commits.message:
[Feature] support MLA attention mode for Kimi-K3.1 DFlash2 draft models (#21675)

Checkpoints such as RadixArk/Kimi-K3.1-Dflash2-Preview declare
`dflash_config.attention_mode="mla"` and store DeepSeek-style MLA draft
weights
(`q_a_proj`/`kv_a_proj_with_mqa`/`kv_a_layernorm`/`kv_b_proj`/`q_b_proj`/`o_proj`),
which the GQA-only `DFlash2Qwen3Attention` cannot load. All five draft
layers of this checkpoint also keep a **1024-token sliding window**,
which the Ascend MLA path previously dropped before it reached the
attention kernel, silently corrupting long-context drafts.

This PR makes the checkpoint serve end-to-end on Ascend and makes the
draft's sliding window actually enforced in decode attention on the
verified TP-only configuration.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

**MLA attention mode** (the original scope):
- Add `DFlash2Qwen3MLADecoderLayer` built on `AscendKimiMLAAttention`,
the same MLA draft attention already used by the Kimi K3 DSpark draft.
- Add `DFlash2Qwen3MLAModel`: extends the stacked weight mapper to fuse
the separate A-projections into `fused_qkv_a_proj`, and writes context
KV into the MLA latent cache via the Ascend MLA prolog/prefill writers.
- Dispatch on `dflash_config.attention_mode` in
`DFlash2Qwen3ForCausalLM` so the existing `DFlash2DraftModel`
registration covers both GQA and MLA drafts.
- Make `get_draft_kv_cache_layer_names`/`get_draft_attn_causal` tolerate
MLA attention modules.

**Sliding-window enforcement** (the acceptance-rate fix):
- Resolve the per-layer window exactly like upstream
`_resolve_layer_attention`: `dflash_config.use_swa` forces SWA on every
layer (even an all-full `layer_types`); otherwise only
`sliding_attention` layers are windowed, with the size from
`dflash_config.swa_window_size` or the top-level `sliding_window`. The
top-level `use_sliding_window`/`max_window_layers` pair is intentionally
not consulted — upstream ignores it, and the resolution must agree with
the attention layers upstream builds from the same config. Like
upstream, a sliding layer without any configured window size raises
`ValueError` at load time instead of silently running window-free; a
zero window passes through as configured.
- The registered Ascend Kimi wrapper forwards the resolved layer window
to `MLAAttention` during construction. The backend selector and MLA
implementation see the same window.
- For a causal window of `W` tokens, the kernel can read the current
token and its `W-1` predecessors. On A3, eligible Kimi K3.1 DFlash2
drafts reuse the device-side MLA tiling from #23221. Both
`get_scheduler_metadata` and `flash_attn_with_kvcache` receive
`causal=True` and `window_size=(W-1, 0)`.
- The A3 path requires a uniform causal MLA window and `flash-attn-npu
>= 0.5.1.post1` with the split-query MLA operators. Eligible A5 drafts
use FlashMLA BAND with `mask_mode=4`, `win_left=W-1`, and `win_right=0`.
Other supported windowed layers use FIA V2 with `sparse_mode=4`,
`pre_tokens=W-1`, and `next_tokens=0`.
- Draft KV cache intentionally keeps full retention for now: DFlash
context precompute writes every context row, so a window-limited cache
would leave rows unread by the windowed decode path but still visible to
the not-yet-windowed draft prefill path. Window-limited caching is a
follow-up.
- The device-side tiling paths share one window schedule across draft
layers. In a heterogeneous draft, windowed layers use FIA and
full-attention layers retain their usual backend selection.
- Decode context parallelism (DCP) handling: DCP selects
`AscendMlaDCPImpl` for every MLA attention group, and that decode path
applies no `pre_tokens` band (`sparse_mode=0` with only the causal spec
mask), so a windowed MLA draft under DCP would silently attend the full
DCP-local KV. Such configs are refused at startup with a clear error —
the same restriction upstream vLLM #68214 encodes by refusing DCP for
windowed DFlash2 drafts. DCP support for windowed drafts is a follow-up.
- Windowed MLA drafts require causal attention. The supported band ends
at the current token, so a non-causal window is rejected at startup.

**Rejection-adjusted draft lengths.** The KV length after rejection sets
the right edge of the causal window. At the model length limit, the
per-request sample position determines how many packed query tokens
remain valid. A3 represents each clipped suffix as a zero-KV segment on
device, so later requests keep their physical token offsets. A5 passes
the valid prefix through `seqused_q`. FIA shares an exact, zero-padded
host length mirror across the metadata builds in each proposal. Padding
keeps slot `-1` in eager execution and FULL graph replay.

**Metadata build flow.** Eager execution and FULL graph replay both
enter the upstream `_build_attn_metadata` hook. The FIA-backed MLA
builder receives exact host lengths. The windowed A3 and A5 builders
read the device lengths directly. On A3, the graph manager refreshes the
captured schedule once per replay.

**Device-length scope**: the K3.1 + DFlash2 device-length fast path (no
per-step CPU length sync) currently covers the verified TP-only
configuration; pipeline parallelism, context parallelism, KV-transfer
(P/D), sparse-KV offload, and adaptive verification stay on exact host
counts, and DCP stays on exact host counts as well (the windowed-DCP
combination is refused above). The policy is registered from the Kimi
K3.1 model state via the upstream `initialize_spec_cpu_length_sync`
extension point, so the runner core stays untouched. Relaxing the gate
to those configurations is a follow-up.

**Aux hidden stream contract** (training/serving alignment):
- `fix(kimi_k3)`: capture the materialized AttnRes aux stream when the
DFlash draft declares `aux_hidden_stream="attn_res"` —
Kimi-K3.1-Dflash2-Preview declares `aux_hidden_stream="attn_res"` with
`target_layer_ids=[7, 23, 51, 67, 83, 91]`, meaning the draft was
trained consuming the AttnRes mixed value (the consumption-layer
`res_proj`/`res_norm` mixture collected at target-layer boundaries), but
Ascend only enabled the materialized capture for `method=="dspark"`, so
DFlash2 served on the residual prefix-sum instead. The contract is now
honored by enabling the AttnRes materialized capture for DFlash2 drafts
that declare it, reusing the same proven capture path as DSpark-Qwen3.
Upstream vLLM has the same AttnRes stream gated behind
`VLLM_KIMI_K3_AUX_ATTN_RES_STREAM` (default off) and never reads the
checkpoint field, so this is not a divergence from upstream — it is
honoring a checkpoint declaration that upstream also effectively ignores
by default.

**Supporting fixes**:
- `fix(kimi_k3)`: load DSA indexer weights into the Ascend indexer stack
— the upstream amd loader renames `.self_attn.indexer.*` to
`.dsa_indexer.*` before lookup, which raises `KeyError` on the first DSA
layer for any Kimi-K3.1 checkpoint with DSA layers; indexer weights
matching a registered Ascend parameter are now consumed in
`AscendKimiLinearModel.load_weights` and reported under their original
checkpoint names.
- `fix(kimi_k3)`: build target embedding on the last PP stage for
target-embed drafts (the `spec_decode_needs_target_embed` contract,
matching upstream llama behavior).
- `fix(dflash2)`: mirror upstream causality resolution exactly
(`_dflash_layer_causal`, including the checkpoint-level `is_causal` flag
that upstream consults first), so the published per-layer causality, the
draft-wide non-causal backend requirement, and the per-layer attention
flags resolved from the same config cannot disagree for any checkpoint.
GQA drafts keep the upstream per-layer resolution; the only behavior
change for existing drafts is the intentional startup refusal below.

**Startup validation for windowed MLA drafts.** Windowed MLA requires
causal attention and a decode context parallel size of one.

**Upstream relation.** This is the Ascend counterpart of
vllm-project/vllm#68214 for the Kimi K3.1 DFlash2 checkpoint. A3
windowed MLA, A5 FlashMLA BAND, and FIA apply the same causal window as
upstream sparse MLA decode.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. `RadixArk/Kimi-K3.1-Dflash2-Preview` (and checkpoints with the same
`dflash_config.attention_mode="mla"` + sliding-window draft layers) now
load and serve on Ascend with correct draft attention on the verified
TP-only configuration. Launching a windowed MLA draft with decode
context parallelism now fails fast at startup instead of silently
dropping the window. Launching a non-causal MLA draft that declares a
sliding window now fails fast at startup instead of silently dropping
the window, and declaring a sliding window without any window size now
fails fast at load time, matching upstream validation.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests added/updated under `tests/ut/` (window resolution from
config covering the upstream
`use_swa`/`swa_window_size`/`layer_types`/`sliding_window` shapes,
heterogeneous window selection, DCP refusal for windowed MLA drafts, the
non-causal window refusal, the missing-window-size error and zero-window
passthrough matching upstream, FlashMLA eligibility at layer
construction, causality resolution parity with upstream including the
`is_causal`-first order, the DFlash aux-stream contract selection
honoring `aux_hidden_stream`, rejection-adjusted host lengths with the
proposal-scoped cache, capped-window valid query prefixes, the
common-hook FULL-replay padding update for FIA-backed GQA and MLA
drafts, and the device-length policy). An A5 single-card e2e test
exercises the BAND decode path (eager and graph replay against a
sliding-window reference at the model length limit).
- On A3 with `flash-attn-npu 0.5.1.post1`, the single-card
`test_a3_dflash_mla_window_replay` checks the 1024-token window against
a reference. Three replays change the valid query counts of two requests
independently, including a fully clipped request and a padded graph row.
The focused A3 suites passed 506 tests (7 skipped). On A5, the BAND
operator and focused suites passed 344 tests against the pinned vLLM
main revision (7 skipped) and 342 against v0.34.0 (9 skipped).
- Earlier manual multi-node e2e on Ascend A5 covered the sliding-window
fix end-to-end (target Kimi-K3.1-Pro, draft Kimi-K3.1-Dflash2-Preview,
TP32, `num_speculative_tokens=7`, long-context workloads); end-to-end
throughput and acceptance for the A5 BAND path are still pending.
- Known unrelated issue observed during long runs: multi-node
`shm_broadcast` pyzmq zero-copy race (`_pickle.UnpicklingError`) is an
upstream vLLM issue (cross-node TP only), not caused by this PR.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: window resolution covers
`use_swa`-forced SWA, `layer_types`-driven windows, the top-level
`sliding_window` fallback, and absent-layer-types configs; backend
selection covers uniform causal windows and mixed windowed/full draft
layers; the aux-stream contract covers `attn_res` / `hidden_states` /
absent declarations; causality resolution covers `is_causal`-first,
`dflash_config.causal` override, and the layer_types fallback; the
device-length gate test pins every unsupported configuration falling
back to exact host counts; rejection coverage includes partial
rejections refreshing the host lengths and the capped-window valid query
prefix.
- [x] **Regression test**. `test_mla_layer_attention_settings` checks
the window and BAND eligibility delivered through the registered Kimi
wrapper. `test_mla_draft_eager_and_acl_get_exact_lengths` checks
rejection-adjusted lengths in eager mode and padded FULL replay. The A3
and A5 single-card replay tests verify the effective window at the model
length limit.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**. Startup rejects non-causal
windowed MLA, windowed MLA with DCP, and sliding-window configs without
a window size.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: tests assert the published
window, the guard behavior, the backend/flag selection, the
rejection-adjusted lengths, and the aux-stream contract, not
implementation trivia.
- [x] **Performance impact**. Windowed decode enforces the 1024-token
context used to train this draft. End-to-end throughput and acceptance
for the A3 device-side tiling and A5 BAND paths have not yet been
measured.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Rejection-adjusted host lengths for DFlash2 MLA draft metadata.
+
+After a rejection the draft FIA sliding window must right-align to the
+accepted context, not the optimistic CPU upper bound. The speculator
+mirrors the per-step device seq_lens to a zero-padded host tensor (the
+DSpark pattern) and builds MLA draft metadata through
+``_build_attn_metadata`` (the upstream hook both eager ``propose()`` and
+FULL-graph replay reach) with ``attn_state=ChunkedPrefill``, so both
+paths emit the exact integer list and take the sliding-window FIA
+branch.
+"""
+
+from contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from typing import Any
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import torch

+import vllm_ascend.worker.v2.spec_decode.dflash.speculator as dflash_speculator_module
+from vllm_ascend.attention.attention_v1 import AscendAttentionState

+from vllm_ascend.attention.mla_v1 import AscendMLABackend, AscendMLADecodeMetadata, AscendMLAImpl, AscendMLAMetadata
+from vllm_ascend.worker.v2.spec_decode.dflash.speculator import AscendDFlashSpeculator, draft_metadata_request_count
+

+    ("impl_cls", "causal", "band", "error"),

+        (AscendMLAImpl, True, False, None),
+        (AscendMLAImpl, True, True, None),
+        (AscendMLAImpl, False, False, "must be causal"),
+        (AscendMlaDCPImpl, True, False, "decode context parallelism"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_windowed_mla_draft_layers(monkeypatch, impl_cls, causal, band, error):

[Doc] Update Qwen3.8-Flash-Next A3 and A5 basic PD deployment (#23392)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Update the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next tutorial's A3 and 950DT (A5) basic PD
deployment examples in Section 5.2 with the reference scripts' serving
settings, while omitting optional single-host communication and
initialization overrides.

- Set A3 Decode `HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024`; retain A3 Prefill
`HCCL_BUFFSIZE=8192` and set `HCCL_BUFFSIZE_EP=4096`.
- Enable Fastokens on A3/A5 Prefill and explicitly clear it on A5
Decode. Add the A3 pinned-memory allocator setting.
- Add hash seeds, inherited communication-state cleanup, and ALL_PROXY
cleanup. Remove the redundant A3 Prefill EP buffer unset; retain it on
A3 Decode and both A5 roles, which do not reset that buffer.
- Omit `ACL_OP_INIT_MODE` and `ASCEND_ENABLE_USE_FABRIC_MEM` from both
roles in both basic PD examples.
- Use default DP RPC settings on A3 and default master address/port
settings on A3 and A5. Keep the DP address explicit for A3 Decode and
both A5 roles (DP > 1); omit it for A3 Prefill (DP1).
- Preserve all existing A5 baseline lines, including DP RPC ports
13388/13389 and their table and guidance. A5 cleanup only omits optional
parameters introduced by this PR; its net diff contains additions only.

Retain the existing checkpoint IDs, API/KV endpoints, HCCL socket
ranges, graph defaults, and maximum model lengths (A3: 262144; A5:
143360). Keep engine-ready timeout at 4800 seconds and A5 HCCL execution
timeout at 3600 seconds. Runtime preparation remains in Section 4 rather
than adding private machine paths or profiling setup.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No runtime/API change; documentation-only corrections to an existing
tutorial. No release note fragment is needed.

### How was this patch tested?

- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `bash -n` for all 19 Bash blocks in Sections 5.1–5.2: passed.
- Parsed all 40 JSON configuration arguments in Sections 5.1–5.2:
passed.
- Verified the A3 review checklist, including removed options and
retained DP address, EP buffer, and hash-seed settings: passed.
- Verified both A5 roles' omitted optional parameters and retained DP2
addresses, original DP RPC ports, EP buffer cleanup, and hash seeds:
passed.
- Compared the A5 basic PD section with the original PR base
(e953b96e1): every baseline line is preserved exactly, and its net diff
contains additions only.
- Full `bash format.sh ci` was attempted via Git Bash but stopped during
markdownlint-cli dependency installation. Full lint and documentation
build remain pending CI.
- NPU deployment and performance: CI testing only. No NPU accuracy or
performance results are claimed.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Documentation-only; no runtime
tests added.
- [x] **Regression test**: Documentation-only.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: Documentation-only.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: No new tests.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: No runtime code changes or performance
claims.

[BugFix] Allow DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark MXFP8 main_proj and DSA wo_a layouts (#21953)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark on a ModelSlim W8A8_MXFP8 checkpoint
(`quant_method: ascend`) built `main_proj` as BF16, so the draft loader
failed on `main_proj.scale`. DSA `wo_a` also needs an ND weight of
`[n_local_groups, hidden, o_lora_rank]` for
`npu_transpose_quant_batchmatmul`. That 3D layout is specific to
DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 and does not belong on the shared MXFP8 linear
method.

This change keeps the quantized `main_proj` contract and serves DeepSeek
V4 and V4.1 MXFP8 linears from one method:

- Read `quant_method` from the draft checkpoint `quantization_config`.
When the checkpoint does not set it, use
`vllm_config.quant_config.get_name()`.
- Pass `vllm_config.quant_config` into `main_proj` when packed-cache ops
are available and the method is `fp8` or `ascend`.
- Register the module as `mtp.0.main_proj` so per-layer quant
descriptions match the checkpoint name.
- Register both `("W8A8_MXFP8", "ds_linear")` and `("fp8", "ds_linear")`
on `AscendW8A8MXFP8DSDynamicLinearMethod`, and remove
`AscendW8A8MXFP8DSRequantizedLinearMethod`. The class stores
`quant_config.get_name()` on `quant_method` and keeps per-group scales
when that name is `ascend`. ModelSlim checkpoints keep per-group uint8
scales. Official FP8 checkpoints still expand block scales, including
32x32 and 128x128; a missing block size uses the runtime group size.
With `--quantization ascend`, every quantized linear on DeepSeek V4 or
V4.1 uses `ds_linear`. Other models stay on `linear`. ModelSlim
description files stay unchanged.
- For `wo_a` with `o_lora_rank > 0`, store ND weight `[n_local_groups,
hidden, o_lora_rank]` and scale `[n_local_groups, K/2, o_lora_rank, 2]`.
Other ModelSlim layers use the shared 2D MXFP8 post-processing. Official
FP8 `wo_a` and `wo_b` keep their post-processing after the block-scale
expansion.
- Set `weight_switch_output_gather_specs` to gather dim 0, matching
`ds_linear`, so PCP full-weight prefill reconstructs the `wo_a` groups.
This path does not restore weights for RL reload.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. A DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark ModelSlim W8A8_MXFP8 (`ascend`) checkpoint
keeps `main_proj` quantized and can load `main_proj.scale`. FP8
`main_proj` still receives the runtime quant config when packed-cache
ops are available. With `--quantization ascend`, DeepSeek V4 and V4.1
W8A8_MXFP8 linears use `("W8A8_MXFP8", "ds_linear")`: `wo_a` is stored
as grouped ND, and PCP output gather uses dim 0. Other models keep the
shared 2D `("W8A8_MXFP8", "linear")` method. Official `--quantization
deepseek_v4_fp8` uses that same `ds_linear` class and still expands
block scales, including 32x32 and 128x128.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit tests added with the bugfix:

- `tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v41_dspark.py`
- `test_draft_constructor_uses_upstream_head_contracts` asserts `prefix
== "mtp.0.main_proj"`.
- `test_draft_main_proj_keeps_modelslim_quant_contract` covers
`quant_method="ascend"` on the checkpoint with no runtime method, and a
runtime method of `ascend` with no checkpoint quantization config.
- `tests/ut/quantization/configs/test_modelslim_config.py`
- `test_deepseek_v4_family_mxfp8_linear_uses_ds_linear` selects
`ds_linear` for `deepseek_v4` and `deepseek_v41`, and `linear` for
another model type.
- `test_get_quant_method_for_linear` keeps a non-DeepSeek quantized
linear on `linear`.
- `tests/ut/quantization/methods/w8a8/test_w8a8_mxfp8.py`
- `test_dsa_wo_a_3d_layout` builds
`AscendW8A8MXFP8DSDynamicLinearMethod` with quant method `ascend` and
checks the ModelSlim 3D `wo_a` weight and scale shapes and values.
- `test_output_sharded_full_weight_prefill_gather` checks that the
ModelSlim DeepSeek path gathers both tensors on dim 0.
- `test_process_weights_uses_checkpoint_block_size` checks official FP8
block-scale expansion for block sizes 32 and 128.
- `test_wo_a_layout_uses_loaded_shard` checks the official FP8 `wo_a`
layout when the quant method is not ModelSlim.
- `tests/ut/quantization/methods/test_mx_weight_format_gate.py`
- `test_w8a8_mxfp8_ds_linear` constructs
`AscendW8A8MXFP8DSDynamicLinearMethod((128, 128))` on both the reject
and accept paths.

```bash
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 pytest -sv tests/ut/quantization/methods/w8a8/test_w8a8_mxfp8.py tests/ut/quantization/methods/test_mx_weight_format_gate.py
```

That command covers the shared-class change. 55 tests passed.

NPU serving run: 8 Ascend950DT cards, data parallel 8, one worker per
card. Device state while the service was up:

| NPU | Worker | Power | Temperature | HBM used / total | This service
process |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | DP0 | 397.8 W | 49°C | 95306 / 98304 MB | 87325 MB |
| 1 | DP1 | 388.4 W | 51°C | 95207 / 98304 MB | 87385 MB |
| 2 | DP2 | 394.4 W | 51°C | 95186 / 98304 MB | 87361 MB |
| 3 | DP3 | 397.1 W | 49°C | 95099 / 98304 MB | 87285 MB |
| 4 | DP4 | 387.6 W | 51°C | 92136 / 98304 MB | 87333 MB |
| 5 | DP5 | 390.3 W | 50°C | 92146 / 98304 MB | 87339 MB |
| 6 | DP6 | 388.7 W | 48°C | 92154 / 98304 MB | 87343 MB |
| 7 | DP7 | 391.0 W | 49°C | 92067 / 98304 MB | 87259 MB |

The checkpoint size in the vLLM logs matches the safetensors file size
on disk. The converted weights are 494.05 GiB, and the original weights
are 475.25 GiB. The converted weights are about 18.80 GiB larger (about
4.0%). Unpacking layers.0.ffn.experts from MXFP4 to BF16 adds 18.98 GiB.
Replacing the FP8-block scales with MXFP8 weight scales adds 0.17 GiB,
while the old per-expert scale tensors that are dropped remove 0.35 GiB.
Together these account for the extra 18.80 GiB.

Accuracy: on GPQA Diamond, the converted MXFP8 weights score **178/198
(89.9%)** (runs used temperature=0.01, top_p=1.0, and did not set
reasoning_effort, using the default value). The original FP8 weights
score **179/198 (90.4%)**, runs used temperature=1.0, top_p=1.0,
max_tokens=131072 and did not set reasoning_effort, using the default
value.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: The DSpark test covers
`quant_method` declared on the checkpoint and declared only on the
runtime quant config. The MXFP8 tests cover one and several `wo_a`
groups, ModelSlim and official FP8 post-processing, official block sizes
32 and 128, and the ModelSlim DeepSeek dim-0 gather.
- [x] **Regression test**:
`test_draft_main_proj_keeps_modelslim_quant_contract` locks the
`main_proj` quant config and the `mtp.0.main_proj` prefix.
`test_dsa_wo_a_3d_layout`, `test_wo_a_layout_uses_loaded_shard`, and
`test_output_sharded_full_weight_prefill_gather` lock the DSA `wo_a`
layout and PCP gather. `test_process_weights_uses_checkpoint_block_size`
locks official FP8 expansion. The existing constructor test also asserts
that prefix.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: This change adds no new
exception path. A BF16 `main_proj` used to drop `main_proj.scale` and
the draft loader failed. For `fp8` and `ascend`, the constructor now
passes the quant config and uses the prefix `mtp.0.main_proj`, so the
scale parameter is created. The constructor tests lock that contract.
They do not replay the old loader failure.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: The new tests check the quant
config object, the module prefix, the selected layer type, and tensor
shapes and values.
- [x] **Performance impact**: The NPU table records power, temperature,
and memory for a DP=8 serving run. No throughput or latency comparison
is attached.

[Feature][Model] Support DeepSeek-V4.1 vision encoder ACL graphs (#21519)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek-V4.1 on Ascend currently encodes images through per-image eager
ViT
and aligner calls. This PR connects the model to the existing encoder
ACL graph
manager so eligible image batches can replay captured encoder execution,
reducing repeated Python dispatch and operator launch overhead.

The implementation reuses the upstream
`DeepseekV4VLEncoderCudaGraphMixin`
introduced and refined in
[vllm#56625](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56625)
and [vllm#58499](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58499):

- Add packed ViT execution with precomputed RoPE inputs and `cu_seqlens`
  boundaries to keep attention isolated between images.
- Add packed aligner execution using gather and masking, preserving the
  channel-major spatial merge and padding for odd image grids.
- Implement Ascend encoder graph configuration for the existing FIA
capture
and replay path. The inherited CUDA backend check rejects a `TORCH_SDPA`
  marker during initialization even though Ascend dispatches to FIA; the
  Ascend configuration avoids that incorrect rejection.
- Reuse existing budget selection, eager fallback, metadata preparation,
and
image-span postprocessing. No model-runner or global patch changes are
needed.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. DeepSeek-V4.1 vision encoder ACL graphs can be enabled with:

```bash
--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true}'
```

The default eager path remains available. Inputs outside captured
budgets fall
back to eager execution. Image delimiter assembly remains outside the
graph.
The installed vLLM must provide the upstream encoder graph mixin.

### Serving benchmark results

User-run before/after measurements for the ViT encoder graph
optimization.
All TTFT values are in milliseconds; lower is better. TTFT reduction is
`(before - after) / before * 100%`; a negative value indicates a
regression.

TTFT reduction |

| 1 | 1024 x 1024 | 702.26 | 636.05 | +9.43% |

| 6 | 448 x 448 | 2240.33 | 1731.16 | +22.73% |
| 6 | 1024 x 1024 | 3139.78 | 2907.47 | +7.40% |

[Performance][BugFix] Optimize DSpark C8 QuantFlashMLA decode and fix shrinking-batch graph replay (#23015)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

- Fuse BF16 projection and RoPE with `npu_mla_prolog_v3` before
converting Q and KV to FP8 for eligible Kimi DSpark C8 decode. With DCP,
gather Q heads before quantization and retain the full current KV chunk
for split attention.
- Fix QuantFlashMLA graph replay when a captured batch shrinks. Reserve
enough metadata rows at capture and split replay padding into spans
within the per-request query limit.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Eligible A5 drafts use fused preprocessing automatically. Shrinking
decode batches can replay within the operator’s query-length limit.

### How was this patch tested?

- 117 attention CPU tests passed at `3f89a67d`, covering graph padding,
C8 preprocessing, DCP and layerwise KV loading.
- Earlier A5 measurements on a 93-layer, eight-expert target: at
TP2/DCP1, mean preprocessing kernel time fell from 134.9 to 90.1 µs per
draft-layer call (55 calls per rank). At TP8/DCP8, both C8 versions
produced identical 64-token outputs across two runs each.
- Full-target eight-node P/D validation remains outstanding.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

---------

Signed-off-by: Zhousiwei <zhousiwei2@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: zsw <zhousiwei2@huawei.com>

[Doc] Fix Volcano Kthena PD disaggregation guide (#23444)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
Fix several issues in the Volcano Kthena PD disaggregation guide:

- Quote the heredoc delimiter (`cat << 'EOF'`) so that `$(POD_NAME)` /
  `$(NAMESPACE)` are not evaluated by the shell as command substitution;
  they are now expanded by Kubernetes.
- Inject `POD_NAME` and `NAMESPACE` into the runtime container through
the
  Downward API, so `--pod $(POD_NAME).$(NAMESPACE)` resolves correctly.
- Set `ModelServer.spec.kvConnector.type` to `mooncake`, matching the
`MooncakeConnectorV1` used by vLLM-Ascend. `nixl` would make KV transfer
fail.
- Document the vLLM-Ascend launch arguments and the
`--kv-transfer-config`
fields (including `kv_role`, `kv_port`, `kv_rank`,
`kv_connector_extra_config`).
- Create the `dev` namespace in the prerequisites, since all example
  manifests are deployed into it.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
Documentation only.

Markdown preview / lint only; no code changes.

[Performance] Remove redundant work from Kimi decode operators (#22346)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR removes three sources of redundant work observed in Kimi K3.1
decode and incorporates the A3 Quantized Lightning Indexer (QLI) score
dtype fix from #22240.

#### Performance changes

1. **MoE: use a plain add for one tensor pair.** The shared MoE combine
adds the same shared and routed tensors directly, replacing the
one-element `torch._foreach_add` call. The measured reduction below is
for the profiled Kimi workload.
   - Implementation: `vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/fused_moe.py`.
2. **Indexer: skip the candidate fills and normalization on eligible A3
sharded DCP.** Pass each query row's rank-local visible KV length into
the pack stage. Plain packing, fused sort/pack, and separate sort
preparation mask padding and empty local prefixes before loading IDs or
scores. They still reject negative IDs and non-finite scores. The QLI
output initialization defaults to enabled and stays enabled when row
metadata is unavailable, including the existing A5 path. Candidate
exchange keeps its existing shape and layout. QLI v2 and v3 keep output
initialization enabled by default. The merge retains the upstream v3
candidate block length input and all four outputs.
- Row metadata and packing: `vllm_ascend/attention/indexer.py`,
`vllm_ascend/attention/context_parallel/sharded_indexer.py`,
`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/sharded_indexer.py`.
- QLI dispatch and optional initialization:
`vllm_ascend/device/device_op.py`,
`csrc/attention/quant_lightning_indexer_v2/quant_lightning_indexer_v2_torch_adpt.h`,
`csrc/torch_binding.cpp`, `csrc/torch_binding_meta.cpp`.
3. **Output projection: write into the supplied result slice.** SFA opts
into `AscendRowParallelLinear.try_forward_into()` for Kimi K3.1 decode.
SFA retains the existing NATIVE_INT8_SPARSE guard, which currently
limits this opt-in to A3. An eligible bias-free, unquantized row
projection without internal reduction uses `matmul(out=...)` to avoid
the explicit result assignment. Other cases keep the existing module
path.
- Linear dispatch: `vllm_ascend/ops/linear.py`. SFA call site:
`vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py`.

#### Bug fix from #22240

A3 QLI with `return_value=1` was returning FP32 scores. This change
restores BF16 output, matching A5. A3 native local candidates
(`return_value=2`) still return FP32 scores. Runtime allocation, Meta
inference and host dtype validation follow the same contract across both
the normal and split-and-merge kernel paths.

The candidate packer widens BF16 scores to FP32 for the existing
exchange format. The combined implementation uses the same pack-time
filtering for both changes, removing the standalone normalization kernel
once. Eligible A3 rows continue to use the no-Fill path with rank-local
visible lengths.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Direct A3 QLI callers using `return_value=1` now receive BF16 score
tensors instead of FP32. Callers that require an FP32 tensor can cast
the scores after the call. The cast preserves the BF16 values. The
supported model paths use the existing configuration.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Decode profiling before #22240 was incorporated

The supplied rank-0 1P1D traces are labeled 128K context and batch size
12. The baseline export contains 13 decode steps and the PR export
contains 11. Both traces show one index-mapping marker and 24 QLI calls
per step. Counts and summed device-kernel durations below are normalized
per decode step.

| Work measured | Baseline | PR build | Reduction per step |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MoE shared and routed output add | 92 `ForeachAddList`, 1.698 ms | 92
replacement `Add`, 0.387 ms | 1.311 ms |
| A3 indexer candidate initialization | 48 `Fill`, 0.370 ms | 0 | 0.370
ms |
| A3 indexer candidate normalization | 24 kernels, 0.303 ms | 0 | 0.303
ms |
| A3 indexer candidate pack | 24 kernels, 0.771 ms | 24 kernels, 0.821
ms | −0.050 ms |
| **A3 indexer, total for the three rows above** | **1.443 ms** |
**0.821 ms** | **0.622 ms** |
| BF16 `o_proj` result copy | 24 `TensorMove`, 0.218 ms | 0 | 0.218 ms |

The MoE comparison matches the `[3, 7168]` output-add calls by shape and
their position in the surrounding MoE sequence, excluding five
same-shape `Add` calls already present in each baseline step. The
indexer `Fill` count is for candidate buffers with shape `[48, 1,
2048]`. Totals use unrounded durations.

For BF16 `o_proj`, each step has 24 matching `MatMulV2` calls after the
attention gate with `[48, 768]` activations and a `[48, 7168]` output.
In the baseline each is followed on the same stream by
`aclnnInplaceCopy` / `TensorMove` before ReduceScatter. The PR trace
goes directly to ReduceScatter. Matmul time per step is similar at 0.409
ms and 0.408 ms. The sum for matmul and result copy falls from 0.627 ms
to 0.408 ms.

The traces use different DCP reduction kernels. That change is outside
this patch. An end-to-end speedup remains unmeasured for this patch.
These captures come from an earlier PR build, before the merge with
upstream `main` and the integration of #22240.

#### Accuracy before #22240 was incorporated

Two GPQA runs with the PR applied scored **93.43%** and **93.94%**. A
GPQA baseline under the same settings and direct A3 output comparisons
are pending. Both scores describe model-level accuracy for the build
before #22240 was integrated.

#### Code verification

For `9bc8cbdd7`, the hardware profile, Linear, SFA forward, and SFA
context-parallel unit test files passed together (468 total) with the
vLLM commit listed below. The Linear test verifies direct dispatch to
the supplied buffer and checks fallback for bias, hooks, TP reduction,
and an invalid output shape.

All QSFA padding and DCP attention packing changes were dropped. The
related source and test files match the PR base, including the existing
post-QSFA padding handling and upstream DCP warmup. On the earlier
revision, 15 sharded-indexer unit tests passed in an isolated CPU run,
the CPU Add and BF16 projection examples matched, and the QLI v2/v3
schemas were checked against upstream.

On the integrated revision (`d6cb13212`), Ruff lint and formatting,
Markdown lint, and Git diff whitespace checks passed. Full local
pre-commit checks were limited by Windows tool setup and the CPU test
run required a local vLLM installation.

The integrated tests cover Meta dtypes for all three return modes, A3
BF16 scores against a CPU reference, and graph replay with Fill disabled
and visibility changing between replays. The [E2E
run](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45572221805)
was triggered for the integrated commit. A3 native tests and a fresh
GPQA and decode profiling comparison remain pending for that build.

#### Triton packing specialization

The three affected kernels use dynamic, non-specialized row counts.
Packing geometry, strides, and sort tiles remain compile-time
parameters. The optional visible lengths add a None and an INT32 pointer
variant for each applicable path. Length values can change between
replays without triggering specialization, while pointer alignment can
vary by row slice. The runtime routing and warmup registration are
unchanged.

For the follow-up at 738a32784, Ruff and Markdown lint passed. The
existing 15 sharded-indexer unit tests passed in an isolated CPU run.
Additional CPU checks verified backward-compatible signatures, tiled
forwarding, and all three dispatch paths with mocked launches. Hardware
nightly results and observed startup and serving compilation counts are
pending.

### Checklist

- [x] Review row coverage, padding and empty local history, collective
shapes, and projection fallbacks.
- [x] Compare available decode traces for the three retained decode
changes.

+    """Compare no-Fill QLI + pack with initialized QLI and an exact CPU oracle."""

+    world, rank, interleave, rows, heads, width, page = 2, 1, 8, 4, 64, 128, 128
+    query = torch.ones(rows, heads, width, dtype=torch.int8, device="npu")
+    # Score for local token i is exactly i+1: (128*(i+1)/1024)*(1/8)*64.
+    key = torch.arange(1, page + 1, dtype=torch.int32).clamp_max(127).to(torch.int8)
+    key = key[:, None].expand(page, width).contiguous().reshape(1, page, 1, width).npu()
+    weights = torch.ones(rows, heads, dtype=torch.float16, device="npu")
+    query_scale = torch.full_like(weights, 1 / 8)
+    key_scale = torch.ones(1, page, 1, 1, dtype=torch.float16, device="npu")
+    starts = torch.tensor([0, 2], dtype=torch.int32, device="npu")
+    global_length = torch.tensor([128], dtype=torch.int32, device="npu")
+    local_length = torch.empty(1, dtype=torch.int32, device="npu")
+    visible = torch.empty(rows, dtype=torch.int32, device="npu")
+    table = torch.zeros(1, 1, dtype=torch.int32, device="npu")
+    dcp = dict(global_seq_lens=global_length, cp_world=world, cp_rank=rank, cp_interleave=interleave)
+
+    def run(initialize_outputs):
+        build_local_lengths(global_length, starts[1:], local_length, visible, world, rank, interleave)
+        metadata = BaseDeviceAdaptor.build_indexer_local_metadata(
+            starts, local_length, num_heads_q=heads, head_dim=width, topk=topk, **dcp
+        )
+        indices, scores = BaseDeviceAdaptor.indexer_select_dcp_candidates(
+            query,
+            weights,
+            key,
+            key_scale,
+            table,
+            starts,
+            local_length,
+            query_scale,
+            qli_metadata=metadata,
+            topk=topk,
+            initialize_outputs=initialize_outputs,
+            **dcp,
+        )
+        packed = pack_local_candidates(
+            indices,
+            scores,
+            world,
+            rank,
+            interleave,
+            visible_lengths=None if initialize_outputs else visible,
+        )
+        return indices, scores, packed
+
+    def check(actual, length, active):
+        assert actual[1].dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        # This reference path retains Fill and does not use the row mask.
+        reference = run(True)[2].cpu()
+        assert torch.equal(actual[2].cpu(), reference)
+        global_ids = (torch.arange(topk) // interleave * world + rank) * interleave + torch.arange(topk) % interleave
+        for row in range(rows):
+            count = int((global_ids < length - active + row + 1).sum()) if row < active else 0
+            ids = reference[row, :, 0]
+            values = reference[row, :, 1].contiguous().view(torch.float32)
+            valid = ids >= 0
+            assert int(valid.sum()) == count
+            assert torch.equal(ids[valid].sort().values.long(), global_ids[:count])
+            assert torch.equal(values[valid].sort().values, torch.arange(1, count + 1).float())
+            assert (ids[~valid] == -1).all() and torch.isneginf(values[~valid]).all()

[Performance][A3][A5] Speed up packed DCP attention output combine (#21605)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The shared DCP attention path merges partial outputs from separate K/V
shards, including an optional local result in split MLA attention. For
BF16 head scatter, this PR decodes each packed LSE once per output row
and reuses the rank weights across all features.

Runtime and warmup launch one Triton kernel. The device profile supplies
a compile-time row mode. A3 processes one row at a time because multirow
loads can lower to nested scalar loops. A5 processes eight rows per tile
to improve memory throughput. Each program owns a contiguous interval.
The same selection applies at every row count.

The optimized path accepts `D <= 512`, output-only combine and unit
local feature stride when a local output is present. Other supported
layouts and dtypes use the existing scalar path.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Packed DCP attention output combine is faster on the target A3 and A5
shapes. Callers use the existing API. The result includes the optional
local contribution once, masks outputs with nonfinite LSE and returns
zeros for all-invalid rows.

### How was this patch tested?

**Device-kernel performance.** The public wrapper ran on the same device
with the same inputs for each comparison. The table gives mean kernel
duration from two interleaved `msprof op` captures per side against
fixed main `6385299e`. Both shapes have 12 local heads, 512 features,
eight received ranks and one token-major local contribution.

| Device | Tokens | main (µs) | PR implementation (µs) | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A3 | 144 | 203.984 | 129.493 | 1.58× |
| A3 | 152 | 205.424 | 135.323 | 1.52× |
| A5 | 144 | 88.958 | 50.473 | 1.76× |
| A5 | 152 | 92.471 | 51.791 | 1.79× |

**Correctness and warmup.** At `6840da5c0`, the single-card DCP suite
passed 25/25 on each device. Four head-scatter cases use independently
encoded inputs and a CPU FP64 reduction, covering a single rank/feature,
received-only and local inputs, head-major strides, tails and invalid or
extreme LSE. The tests require finite output, at least 99% of elements
within `2e-5 + 0.004 * abs(reference)`, and maximum absolute error at
most 0.02.

Runtime and warmup select the same JIT function and mode. The device
contributes one mode per installation. Rank count, feature block size,
local contribution, pointer alignment and ordinary scalar specialization
can still produce variants. The two routing and warmup unit-test files
passed on the published head (41 tests). The A5 validation also passed
33 selected routing/warmup tests at `6840da5c0`.

Device tests and the timings above used `6840da5c0`. The published head
adds a kernel comment, removes a redundant terminal return and two
overlapping host test parameters, and condenses the documentation. The
single-card suite and kernel arithmetic are identical. Model-level
accuracy and throughput, distributed HCCL performance, and serving-time
compilation counts were not measured in this run.

Model level performance gains about 1.7ms with KimiK3.1.
```bash
pytest -q tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_dcp_a2a.py
pytest -q tests/ut/ops/test_dcp_a2a_combine.py tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/test_kernel_warmup.py
```

### Checklist

- [x] Input boundaries, invalid LSE and independent-reference accuracy
- [x] Public-entry device timings on A3 and A5
- [x] Runtime and warmup mode selection
- [x] Operator documentation and release note
- [x] Full CI and model-level validation

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

commits.message:
[Doc][Recipe] Configure Kimi-K3 Ascend variants and 950DT MXFP 4P4D (#19991)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

- Use `Eco-Tech/Kimi-K3-w4a8` on Ascend 910C and
`Eco-Tech/Kimi-K3-w4a8-mxfp-QuaRot` on Ascend 950DT. The 950DT MXFP
checkpoint is publicly available on
[ModelScope](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/Kimi-K3-w4a8-mxfp-QuaRot).
The Recipes sizing estimate is 1823 GB, calculated from the indexed
tensor size with 20% headroom.
- Configure an eight-host 950DT MXFP 4P4D preset with direct
MooncakeConnectorV2 KV transfer. Prefill defaults to TEP (TP8 with
expert parallelism), with DP1, PP4, and layer partition `24,24,24,21`.
P0 exposes the Prefill API and P1–P3 join as headless pipeline stages.
Decode uses DP4 / TP8 / DCP8 with one external DP rank and HTTP endpoint
per host. The Ascend Router defaults to port 1999 and lists P0 and the
four Decode endpoints.
- Set `--max-model-len 1048576` on both pools and enable DCP8 on Decode,
as specified for 950DT in [section 5.3 of the Kimi-K3
tutorial](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/tutorials/models/Kimi-K3.html#53-long-context-and-1m-pd-separation-deployment).
The preset uses 32 sequences and DSpark with seven draft tokens. Prefill
uses eager execution at 0.80 memory utilization and Decode uses
`FULL_DECODE_ONLY` at 0.90.
- The 950DT Install tab uses `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.32.0rc1-a5`
with a per-host Docker pull note. The generated 910C and 950DT container
commands both specify `vllm serve`.
- Document `--headless` for mixed-serving followers and the Mooncake
library and proxy setup for manual worker startup.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

The command builder offers the 950DT MXFP 4P4D 1M preset and the 950DT
MXFP mixed-serving path. The 910C mixed-serving path uses W4A8. The
patch only changes the Kimi-K3 recipe overlay.

### How was this patch tested?

- Passed overlay assembly, schema validation, and JSON API generation
for all 237 models using Recipes renderer `b5c6ea1`.
- Verified that all eight generated worker commands set the 1M limit and
that the four Decode workers use DCP8. Checked the PP4 and Mooncake
topology, per-host networking, five Router endpoints, and Router port
1999.
- Cross-checked the MXFP checkpoint index against the shard headers and
recalculated the sizing estimate.
- `git diff --check` passed.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

Signed-off-by: MAyang38 <mafajun0328@gmail.com>

+          - '--decode-context-parallel-size'
+          - '8'
+          - '--block-size'
+          - '768'
+          - '--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size'
+          - '768'
+          - '--max-num-batched-tokens'
+          - '768'
+          - '--gpu-memory-utilization'
+          - '0.90'
+          - '--compilation-config'
+          - '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
+          - '--additional-config'
+          - '{"enable_mlapo":true,"multistream_overlap_shared_expert":true,"scheduler_config":{"recompute_scheduler_enable":true}}'
+        remove_args:
+          - '--data-parallel-hybrid-lb'
+          - '--no-enable-prefix-caching'
+        env:
+          HCCL_IF_IP: $DECODE_NODE_1
+          VLLM_HOST_IP: $DECODE_NODE_1
+        json_args:
+          '--kv-transfer-config':
+            MooncakeConnectorV2:
+              kv_port: 30300
+    runbook: |
+      Assign `PREFILL_NODE_1` through `PREFILL_NODE_4` and `DECODE_NODE_1` through
+      `DECODE_NODE_4` to the hosts' data-network IPs. Set `IFACE_NAME` to the
+      data interface.
+
+      Before starting vLLM manually, add the Mooncake library directory
+      inside each worker container.
+
+      ```bash
+      export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/latest/python/site-packages/mooncake${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"
+      ```
+
+      If an HTTP proxy is configured, include the worker and Router addresses
+      in both `NO_PROXY` and `no_proxy` for direct HTTP traffic between hosts.
+
+      Start all four Prefill pipeline stages with the shared rendezvous at
+      `PREFILL_NODE_1:41000`. Only the rank-0 Prefill node serves HTTP on port
+      8000. Start one Decode DP rank per host with `DECODE_NODE_1:12321` as the
+      DP coordinator. All four Decode ranks serve HTTP on port 8000. Mooncake
+      KV port bases are 30100 for Prefill and 30300 for Decode.
+
+      Stage the Kimi-K3 MXFP checkpoint and the Kimi-K3 DSpark draft on every
+      host. If serving from disk, mount both directories at the same container
+      paths on every host and substitute those paths for the model IDs in the
+      worker commands. Once all eight workers are healthy, start the Ascend
+      Router on port `1999`, then send a request with model `kimi-k3` and
+      confirm KV transfer.
+
+      Section 5.3 of the linked tutorial configures 1,048,576 tokens for input
+      and output combined and enables DCP8 on Decode. Reserve space for the
+      generated response when validating long-context requests.
+
+hardware_notes:
+  ascend_950dt:
+    title: Checkpoint memory estimate
+    body: The 1823 GB estimate uses the indexed MXFP checkpoint tensor size plus 20% headroom, rounded up.
+
+guide_sections:
+  section1: |
+    ## Ascend mixed Prefill/Decode deployment
+
+    For the four-node A3/A5 mixed deployment, follow the
+    [official mixed deployment reference](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/vllm-ascend-cn/zh-cn/latest/tutorials/models/Kimi-K3.html#51-prefilldecode)
+    for the per-node launch commands, communication settings, and startup order.
+    Only node 0 serves HTTP. Append `--headless` to the generated commands for
+    nodes 1–3.
+
+    Download the [A3 W4A8](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/Kimi-K3-w4a8)
+    or [950DT MXFP](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/Kimi-K3-w4a8-mxfp-QuaRot)
+    checkpoint from ModelScope. The worker environment uses ModelScope for
+    model IDs, including the draft model when speculative decoding is enabled.
+
+    The 950DT MXFP 4P4D preset provides a separate eight-node configuration
+    with direct Mooncake KV transfer. See the preset runbook for startup and
+    verification steps.

commits.message:
[Doc][Recipe] Add Kimi-K2.6 Ascend W4A8 deployment recipe (#21280)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add the Kimi-K2.6 Ascend overlay in
`recipes/overlays/moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6.yaml`, following the source
ownership policy in recipes PR #1208. Replaces #20795.

- Add the ModelScope `Eco-Tech/Kimi-K2.6-w4a8` checkpoint for Ascend
910C and 950DT.
- Pin vLLM-Ascend 0.30.0 A3/A5 images and provide hardware-specific
source installation instructions.
- Configure the 910C single-node DEP reference with TP4 × DP4 + EP and
the official tutorial's runtime settings.
- Keep speculative decoding off by default; use DFlash on 910C and the
contributor-reported Eagle3 configuration with one speculative token on
950DT when explicitly enabled.
- Add hardware notes, prerequisites, launch guidance and references.
Explain the served model name to use in the shared client example.

This overlay uses the current renderer schema. It no longer depends on
recipes #1243 or vLLM #66389: Guide sections append when owner insertion
markers are absent; optional owner layout improvements can land
independently.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes: Ascend W4A8 recipe choices, commands, installation instructions and
Guide content.

Only W4A8 (Ascend) is covered. The current renderer cannot disable
inherited variants per hardware from an overlay. Unsupported `support:
unsupported` fields have been removed; inherited GPU variants may remain
visible on Ascend. Hardware notes explicitly tell users to select W4A8.
No GPU variant allowlist or shared GPU behavior is changed.

The 714 GB memory requirement remains an estimate. Official 910C
tutorial evidence and contributor-reported 950DT Eagle3 validation do
not establish support for every generated combination. The 950DT draft
path is a placeholder and must be replaced with the actual Eagle3
checkpoint directory.

### How was this patch tested?

Against unmodified renderer schema/command logic from recipes main
`46e1415`, without #1243:

- Official `validate-source.mjs --source vllm-ascend`: strict source
assembly, schema validation and full JSON API generation passed (236
models, 1,848 per-hardware renderings).
- Ascend configuration checker for Kimi-K2.6: 27 scenarios, 0 errors and
35 warnings. Warnings include inherited variants falling back to GPU
installation defaults and PD configurations without independent
expectations; these are not runtime validation.
- Focused checks passed for A3/A5 image selection, ModelScope, DEP
arguments, default speculative decoding off and explicit DFlash/Eagle3
selection.
- Existing GPU variants and rendered commands on H200, B300 and MI355X
are unchanged.
- YAML parsing and `git diff --check` passed.
- Windows validation used CI copy mode and a local filesystem-only
adapter for copy/cleanup incompatibilities; schema, source merge and
command generation logic were unchanged. Validation helpers are not
included in this PR.
- Local `bash format.sh ci` could not complete because pre-commit is not
installed; remote format/CI results remain required.
- No new NPU installation, inference or performance tests were
performed.

Source tutorial:
https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/tutorials/models/Kimi-K2.6.html

AI assistance was used.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

---------

Signed-off-by: CuiZ2007 <zhengcui2007@outlook.com>

+                use_ascend_direct: true
+                prefill: {pp_size: null}
+                decode: {pp_size: null}
+          # Only edits an enabled speculative feature; off stays off.
+          --speculative-config:
+            method: eagle3
+            model: lightseekorg/kimi-k2.6-eagle3
+            num_speculative_tokens: 3
+    points:
+      one_p_one_d:
+        label: 1P1D - TP8 / local DP2 per node
+        default: true
+      internal_dp:
+        label: 1P1D - internal DP, one HTTP endpoint per node
+        description: >-
+          One dedicated node per role; native internal load balancing replaces
+          the per-rank HTTP endpoints. This is an unvalidated adaptation.
+        roles:
+          prefill: {data_parallel_lb: internal}
+          decode: {data_parallel_lb: internal}
+      distributed_dp:
+        label: Two-node pools - TP4 / global DP8 per role
+        description: >-
+          Four A3 nodes total: one two-node Prefill pool and one two-node Decode
+          pool, each TP4/local DP4/global DP8. Unlike the tutorial's independent
+          Prefill replicas, all Prefill ranks here join one DP group. This
+          topology adaptation requires separate end-to-end validation.
+        roles:
+          prefill: {nodes: 2, tp: 4, data_parallel_lb: external}
+          decode: {nodes: 2, tp: 4, data_parallel_lb: external}
+    runbook: |
+      ## Scope and prerequisites
+
+      Reference design only. The official tutorial recommends MindIE Motor
+      plus vLLM-Ascend for production. Its 1P1D tuning example uses TP8/DP2 on
+      each 16-NPU A3 node. Native external/internal DP and the distributed-pool
+      point are adaptations, not Kimi-K2.6 runtime-validation claims.
+
+      Use dedicated Prefill and Decode hosts, the W4A8 checkpoint, matching
+      vLLM/vLLM-Ascend 0.30.0 environments, Mooncake and the proxy script from
+      that same runtime. Check `vllm serve --help` for the multi-port and
+      supervisor flags. Configure each node's NIC variables (GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME,
+      TP_SOCKET_IFNAME and HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME) for its own interconnect.
+
+      ## Start workers, then the proxy
+
+      1. Fill the generated node addresses and DP RPC / worker ports; use each
+         node's distinct exported command, including start ranks 0 and 4 for
+         the two-node pools. Do not repeat the first node's command everywhere.
+      2. Run the native `vllm serve` commands on every node. No
+         `launch_online_dp.py` or `run_dp_template.sh` is needed. External local
+         DP>1 uses `--data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb`; each local rank
+         listens on base_port + local_rank. Internal DP uses one HTTP endpoint
+         per role and is offered only for the one-node pools.
+      3. Keep supervisor health port 8290 free on each host. Multi-port mode
+         starts it automatically; it is not a model-serving port. Keep it
+         distinct from worker HTTP, DP RPC and KV ports. Dedicated hosts allow
+         the same supervisor port on different nodes.
+      4. Once every worker/rank is healthy, start the generated Ascend Router
+         command. Its preset port is 1999; send client, verification and
+         benchmark requests through that port, not through the supervisor.
+      5. Verify /v1/models and an actual completion through the Router, then
+         confirm Mooncake KV transfer in logs. Repeat for each topology before
+         declaring it verified. No accuracy or performance result is implied.
+
+      Speculative decoding is off by default. If enabled, Prefill remains
+      non-speculative and Decode uses the tutorial's Eagle3 draft with three
+      tokens; download that separate draft checkpoint first. That path also
+      needs a compatible runtime and Kimi-K2.6 validation.

[Doc] Resolve AIDD scan findings in documentation (#23407)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix multiple minor documentation issues detected by AIDD static scan,
including wording ambiguity, grammar, formatting and description
consistency problems.
These changes improve readability and accuracy of Ascend deployment
docs, with no functional code change.

### Does this PR introduce *any* user-facing change?

No, this is documentation-only update.

### How was this patch tested?

Manual preview in Mintlify; verified rendering, wording and link
references. No code/benchmark test required.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

[CI] Remove all GLM-5.1 cases from the nightly matrix (#23520)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Removes all GLM-5.1 cases from the nightly matrix (A2, A3 and A3-560T
pools):

- `multi-node-GLM-5.1-w8a8-A2` (a2 multi_node) — commit e259fc406
- `multi-node-GLM-5.1-W8A8C8-MTP-A3_198k_function` (a3 double_node)
- `multi-node-GLM-5.1-W8A8C8-A3_128k_90_50` (a3 double_node)
- `glm-5.1-w8a8-prefill-mc2` (a3-560t single_node)

After this change the nightly matrix has no GLM-5.1 registration left
(the A5 `GLM5_1_W4A4_A5` entry is a different GLM-5.1 w4a4c8
quantization on A5 hardware and is not covered by this PR). GLM-5.1
coverage remains on the weekly matrix (13 registrations on A3), where
the long-context PD scenarios of this model family are concentrated.

Test-only config change: no source code or test assets are modified.

## Related issues

None.

## Test cases passed

Config-only removal; YAML validated — a2.multi_node 2 -> 1,
a3.double_node 8 -> 7, a3-560t.single_node 20 entries, no other GLM-5.x
cases touched.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

---------

Signed-off-by: CuixyHW <cuixuanyu1@huawei.com>

[BugFix] Include PCP in DP supervisor device sharding (#23428)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

With `--data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb`, the DP supervisor in vLLM
v0.34.0 assigns each child `TP × PP` devices. An Ascend worker with PCP
enabled needs `TP × PP × PCP`. For example, with TP=2, PP=1 and PCP=2,
the second local DP rank receives devices `[2, 3]` and can fail its
device-count check during startup.

Backport the upstream device-slicing fix in the supervisor process. It
gives the second rank `[4, 5, 6, 7]` in this example and preserves the
order of an explicit `--device-ids` list. The patch is installed only
when the upstream helper exhibits the old behavior. It can be removed
once both Ascend's release and verified-main vLLM pins include the fix.
[Upstream PR #69664](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69664)

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Multi-port external load balancing assigns the full set of NPUs to
each local DP rank when PCP is enabled. Existing launch commands pick up
the fix automatically.

### How was this patch tested?

Ran the new tests in
`tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_dp_supervisor.py` in an isolated CPU
harness. It loads each revision's full DP supervisor and the Ascend
platform patch registration, with service and hardware dependencies
stubbed.

| vLLM revision | Before the backport | With Ascend patch registration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v0.34.0 and verified main `c410543d` | 3 failed, 1 passed on each |
All 4 new cases and 3 existing upstream cases passed on each |
| Upstream merge `778bef28` | All 4 new cases passed | All 4 new cases
and 4 existing upstream cases passed. The native helper stayed active |

Run the regression tests in the standard Ascend test environment with
this command.

```sh
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 pytest -q tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_dp_supervisor.py
```

Hardware validation is pending. The local checks ran on CPU.

`bash format.sh ci` passed. The English documentation also passed the
strict MkDocs build (`DOCS_LANG=en bash tools/rtd_build.sh`).

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage** — covered adjacent local DP
ranks, PCP=1, PCP=2 and a partial final shard.
- [x] **Regression test** — reproduced the failure on both Ascend
dependency pins.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage** — verified the requested range
in the error for a short device list.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests** — asserted the device IDs passed
to each child by the upstream launcher.
- [ ] **Performance impact** — the change runs during launcher setup.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+from argparse import Namespace
+
+from vllm.entrypoints.launchers import dp_supervisor
+
+
+def _build_device_ids(args: Namespace, local_rank: int) -> list[int | str]:
+    """Give each DP child its TP × PP × PCP slice of the visible devices."""
+    # v0.34 callers can omit PCP when using its default.
+    pcp_size = getattr(args, "prefill_context_parallel_size", 1)
+    devices_per_rank = args.tensor_parallel_size * args.pipeline_parallel_size * pcp_size
+    start = local_rank * devices_per_rank
+    stop = start + devices_per_rank
+    device_ids = getattr(args, "device_ids", None)
+    if device_ids is not None:
+        if stop > len(device_ids):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"--device-ids has {len(device_ids)} entries, but DP rank {local_rank} needs devices [{start}, {stop})"
+            )
+        return device_ids[start:stop]
+    return list(range(start, stop))
+
+
+# The release and verified-main pins advance independently. Only replace a
+# supervisor that gives a two-rank PCP group a single device (vLLM #69664).
+if dp_supervisor._build_device_ids(
+    Namespace(tensor_parallel_size=1, pipeline_parallel_size=1, prefill_context_parallel_size=2, device_ids=None),
+    local_rank=0,
+) == [0]:
+    dp_supervisor._build_device_ids = _build_device_ids

[Performance][MoE] Quantize W8A8 activations before PCP AllGather (#22230)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The Ascend MoE ALLGATHER path gathers floating-point activations across
prefill context-parallel (PCP) ranks. Each rank then quantizes the
gathered rows during expert dispatch. For W8A8 INT8 and A5 W8A8 MXFP8
MoE, this change quantizes local padded rows before PCP AllGather. Each
rank gathers the activations together with their per-token INT8 scales
or per-block MXFP8 scales in matching row order. The existing Ascend
routing kernel consumes both tensors. Router logits retain their
existing gather, and DP still gathers before PCP.

The PCP optimization keeps floating-point inputs for LoRA, custom
routing functions, and layers that apply router weights to the input.
The existing EP sequence-parallel path continues to apply its own
quantization policy.

Upstream vLLM already uses the same ordering for eligible FP8 and NVFP4
kernels. This PR applies it to Ascend's W8A8 INT8 and MXFP8 paths, which
handle preparation and routing via `torch_npu`. [Upstream MoE
runner](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0c4fe70662363193189f2212ecd9d55d39d5349e/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py)

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Eligible W8A8 prefill workloads transfer fewer activation bytes and
avoid repeated quantization across PCP ranks. This applies automatically
with the existing configuration. The standalone and fused CANN
quantizers can differ by one INT8 quantization step.

### How was this patch tested?

- At `a18c97025`, the single two-rank PCP regression passed in 29.86 s
on two Ascend 950DT NPUs with CANN 9.3.0, torch-npu 2.10.0.post7 and
pinned vLLM `c410543d9fff`.
- The test gathers floating-point rows for the dispatch baseline and
compares them with quantization before the real HCCL gather. INT8 covers
local token counts (0, 5) and (4096, 4095), including zero padding and
8192 gathered rows. Routing indices and expert counts matched exactly,
and the routed INT8 activations matched within one quantization step.
- On A5 the same test also exercises both baseline MXFP8 dispatch paths
for (17, 9) and (0, 5) local tokens. The routed E4M3 payload and E8M0
block scales matched byte for byte. Both the default two-card selector
and the `ready-a5` suite select the shared test. The model accuracy and
throughput measurements below apply to the earlier INT8 candidate.

  ```bash
pytest -q
tests/e2e/pull_request/two_card/ops/test_pcp_quantized_routing.py
  ```

#### Hardware and software

The earlier candidate ran on DeepSeek-V4-Flash W8A8 with 32 Ascend 910B3
devices, two prefill replicas (TP1/PCP8/EP8, max batched tokens 8192,
max sequences 16) and two decode replicas (DP16/EP16 with DSpark, five
draft tokens). The stack used CANN 9.2.0, PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu, and
torch-npu 2.10.0.post7. A used the baseline serving image. B applied the
two MoE method changes to the prefill workers on the same image. These
measurements predate the rebase.

#### Correctness

On NPU, the standalone INT8 quantizer followed by prequantized dispatch
matched fused quantization on routing indices and expert token counts
for 1, 17, 1024, and 8192 tokens, including all-zero padding rows. Valid
routed INT8 values differed by at most one quantization step, and the
maximum absolute scale difference was 3.73e-9.

The model accuracy A/B used the same prompts and scorer for both
variants. Each arm completed all 2,737 requests without HTTP errors.
Standard tasks ran at temperature 0 with a fixed output budget of 4,096
tokens. Truncated, empty, and unparseable answers counted as incorrect.
The retrieval test used approximately 8K, 32K, and 64K inputs at three
insertion depths, with eight prompts per combination.

| Dataset | A baseline | B candidate | B − A (percentage points) |
Paired 95% interval (percentage points) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K test | 1,278/1,319 (96.89%) | 1,278/1,319 (96.89%) | 0.00 |
[−0.68, +0.68] |
| C-Eval validation | 1,194/1,346 (88.71%) | 1,201/1,346 (89.23%) |
+0.52 | [−0.74, +1.78] |
| Long-context retrieval | 72/72 | 72/72 | 0.00 | — |

Both standard tasks met the predefined regression criterion of a paired
95% lower bound of at least −1 percentage point. Retrieval had zero
candidate-only failures. In a diagnostic rerun at an 8,192-token output
budget, A answered 74/144 correctly and B answered 83/144. That subset
consisted of the union of truncation or answer-extraction failures from
both arms. Individual answers differed between arms.

#### E2E performance, fixed-workload A/B

Each setting used three fixed prompt bursts, temperature 0, and
`ignore_eos`. The 32K/32 and 8K/16 bursts generated 64 tokens per
request. The 32K/1 burst issued four sequential requests that generated
32 tokens each. The final comparison had zero prefix-cache hits and
preemptions, with all 156 requests per variant succeeding. Prompt
throughput uses input tokens divided by full burst wall time, including
generation.

| Prompt length / concurrency | Mean prefill, A → B | Mean TTFT, A → B |
E2E prompt throughput, A → B (tok/s) |

| 32K / 32 | 1.554 → 1.503 s (−3.3%) | 14.524 → 14.096 s (−2.9%) |
36,443 → 38,256 (+5.0%) |

25,634 (+3.7%) |

11,080 (+6.6%) |

A and B used the same node pool, with prefill and decode placement
varying between variants. Earlier B runs that reused decode processes

followed a decode restart and warmup.

#### E2E performance, long-context multi-turn candidate runs

EvalScope generated 96 random sessions per run at concurrency 32, with

inputs, and up to 1,024 output tokens per turn (`ignore_eos`, streaming,

| B3 | 690 | 698.74 | 1,011.20 | 131,000.91 | 17.59 | 32.13 | 15.24 |

Total throughput includes cached input tokens. KV cache hit is the

+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.multiprocessing as mp
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import (
+    destroy_distributed_environment,
+    destroy_model_parallel,
+    init_distributed_environment,
+    initialize_model_parallel,
+)

+from vllm.utils.network_utils import get_open_port
+
+from vllm_ascend.ascend_config import init_ascend_config
+from vllm_ascend.ascend_forward_context import _EXTRA_CTX
+from vllm_ascend.ops.fused_moe.dataclass.moe_quant import MoEMxfpParams, MoEQuantParams
+from vllm_ascend.ops.fused_moe.dataclass.router_input import MoeRouterInput
+from vllm_ascend.ops.fused_moe.dataclass.token_dispatcher import MoETokenDispatchInput
+from vllm_ascend.ops.fused_moe.moe_utils import maybe_normalize_mxfp_scale_layout
+from vllm_ascend.ops.fused_moe.prepare_finalize import PrepareAndFinalizeWithAllGather
+from vllm_ascend.ops.fused_moe.token_dispatcher import TokenDispatcherWithAllGather
+from vllm_ascend.quantization.quant_type import QuantType
+from vllm_ascend.quantization.utils import DynamicMXQuantScaleAlg
+from vllm_ascend.utils import AscendDeviceType, get_ascend_device_type
+
+
+def _compare_routing(rank, counts, quant, hidden_size=512):
+    # Vary magnitude across ranks and blocks so swapping scales changes the output.
+    torch.manual_seed(22230 + rank)
+    x = torch.randn(counts[rank], hidden_size, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    block_magnitudes = (2.0 ** (torch.arange(hidden_size // 32) % 7 - 3)).repeat_interleave(32)
+    x = (x * block_magnitudes).bfloat16().npu()
+    logits = torch.randn(counts[rank], 8).npu()
+    _EXTRA_CTX.max_tokens_across_pcp = max(counts)
+    layer = PrepareAndFinalizeWithAllGather(SimpleNamespace(is_sequence_parallel=False, pcp_size=2, dp_size=1))
+    baseline = layer.prepare(x, logits)
+    actual = layer.prepare(x, logits, quant_type=quant.quant_type)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual.router_logits, baseline.router_logits, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    assert actual.hidden_states.dtype == quant.get_dst_type
+    assert actual.pertoken_scale is not None
+
+    # All experts are local, so every gathered row (including padding) is checked after routing.
+    dispatcher = TokenDispatcherWithAllGather(top_k=2, num_local_experts=8)
+    weights, ids = baseline.router_logits.topk(2)
+
+    def dispatch(prepared):
+        return dispatcher.token_dispatch(
+            MoETokenDispatchInput(
+                hidden_states=prepared.hidden_states,
+                topk_weights=weights,
+                topk_ids=ids.int(),
+                routing=MoeRouterInput(None, 0, None, False, pertoken_scale=prepared.pertoken_scale),
+                quant=quant,
+            )
+        )
+
+    routed, expected = dispatch(actual), dispatch(baseline)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(routed.combine_metadata.expanded_row_idx, expected.combine_metadata.expanded_row_idx)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(routed.group_list, expected.group_list)
+    if quant.is_mxfp:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(routed.hidden_states.view(torch.uint8), expected.hidden_states.view(torch.uint8))
+        expected_scale = maybe_normalize_mxfp_scale_layout(expected.dynamic_scale)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(routed.dynamic_scale.view(torch.uint8), expected_scale.view(torch.uint8))
+    else:
+        # Standalone and fused INT8 quantizers can differ by one rounding step.
+        torch.testing.assert_close(routed.hidden_states, expected.hidden_states, rtol=0, atol=1)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(routed.dynamic_scale, expected.dynamic_scale, rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-8)
+
+
+def _worker(rank, port):
+    torch.npu.set_device(rank)
+    config = VllmConfig()
+    with set_current_vllm_config(config):
+        init_ascend_config(config)
+        init_distributed_environment(2, rank, f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{port}", rank, backend="hccl")
+        try:
+            initialize_model_parallel(prefill_context_model_parallel_size=2, backend="hccl")
+            with override_forward_context(create_forward_context(None, config)):
+                int8 = MoEQuantParams(quant_type=QuantType.W8A8)
+                _compare_routing(rank, (0, 5), int8)
+                _compare_routing(rank, (4096, 4095), int8, hidden_size=4096)
+                if get_ascend_device_type() == AscendDeviceType.A5:
+                    mxfp8 = MoEQuantParams(
+                        quant_type=QuantType.W8A8MXFP, mxfp=MoEMxfpParams(act_quant_type=torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+                    )
+                    for scale_alg in DynamicMXQuantScaleAlg:
+                        get_forward_context().additional_kwargs["dynamic_mx_quant_scale_alg"] = scale_alg
+                        for counts in ((17, 9), (0, 5)):
+                            _compare_routing(rank, counts, mxfp8)
+        finally:
+            destroy_model_parallel()
+            destroy_distributed_environment()
