[Performance][PCP] Reduce short-prefill replication and MegaMoE buffer reservations (#22983)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

With prefill context parallelism (PCP) and decode context parallelism
(DCP) enabled, an empty tail chunk could cause every rank to process an
entire prefill request. For example, a 225-token prefill on PCP8 fills
fifteen 15-token chunks and leaves the sixteenth empty. Reserving
capacity for 64 such requests inflates the target startup profile and
the prefill MC2/MegaMoE buffer.

In the Ascend MRV2 PCP manager, each rank keeps its full-width head
chunk. When fixed-width slicing would leave an empty tail, the manager
distributes the remaining tokens across the tails if all ranks can
receive one. A 225-token prefill then gives each rank 28 or 29 tokens.
Every rank has two chunks with a longest chunk of 15, so the sparse
Indexer derives the same planning charge of 30 on every rank. Dispatch,
KV write deduplication and hidden-state restoration use this layout
through the existing PCP manager interfaces.

For PCP size `P > 1`, the largest prefill that still needs replication
is `3P - 1`: at that length the heads consume `2P` tokens and only `P -
1` tail tokens remain. The startup budget uses that bound together with
speculative verification length, rounding and the existing prefill graph
floor. This follows up on #21985 and #22656.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Short prefills with PCP and DCP can do less replicated work, and
the local prefill MC2/MegaMoE reservation can shrink. With eager
execution, PCP8/DCP8, TP1, 64 sequences, 16,384 batched tokens and three
DSpark speculative tokens, the target and prefill MC2 budget changes
from **14,776 to 3,464 rows**. DSpark retains its 16,384-row global
context budget. The change applies to the shared Ascend MRV2 path and
requires no new configuration.

At a global `--max-num-batched-tokens` of 24,576, the same eager
configuration reduces the prefill MegaMoE row limit from **15,800 to
4,488 per rank**. The CANN 9.3 A5 planner estimates **7.68 GiB less
communication and workspace reservation per rank** (1.29 GiB
communication and 6.40 GiB workspace, rounded independently). This
leaves room for transient allocations while serving larger batches with
MegaMoE enabled. The global scheduler limit and the draft model's global
context budget continue to follow the configured token budget.

### How was this patch tested?

Compared with Ascend main `a3020ab6149f`. The following are **CPU layout
and budget results**. The row counts describe the largest PCP rank in a
batch.

| Scheduled batch on PCP8/DCP8 | Base | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| One 225-token prefill | 225 | 29 |
| 64 prefills of 225 tokens each | 14,400 | 1,856 |
| 63 prefills of 23 tokens plus one of 14,935 | 3,317 | 3,317 |

- Ran `pytest -q tests/ut/worker/test_pcp_manager_v2.py
tests/ut/worker/test_pcp_profile_budget.py
tests/ut/test_ascend_forward_context.py` in a Linux CPU test
environment. With the repository's verified vLLM revision
`c410543d9fff`, **424 passed**. With deployment revision `4ba787ec9959`,
**417 passed, 7 skipped**.
- Verified the mixed Decode/Prefill layout, original positions, uniform
Indexer planning charge, canonical KV writes, hidden-state restoration,
graph capture floor and prefill MC2 capacity. An additional
eight-process CPU/Gloo all-gather test passed for three mixed or
boundary batches.
- The full CPU suite passed against both vLLM revisions on commit
`192fa3a49`. The verified revision passed 22,344 tests with 131 skipped.
Release `v0.33.0` passed 22,254 with 156 skipped. [CPU CI
logs](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45237709673)

#### CPU CI and hardware correctness (2026-11-26)

- On `c8c30d2`, pre-commit and both full CPU unit-test suites passed.
The pinned vLLM main revision passed **23,770** tests with 131 skipped,
and vLLM `v0.34.0` passed **23,765** tests with 136 skipped. [Pinned
main CPU
log](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45825240401/job/139929563835)
· [v0.34.0 CPU
log](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45825240401/job/139929563761)
- On four A3 cards, both vLLM revisions passed **all nine tests** in
`four_card/context_parallel/test_accuracy_v2.py` on `c8c30d2`. The
DeepSeek-V3.2 SFA PCP2/DCP4 case exercised an uncached nine-token
prefill and passed the original exact three-output golden assertion.
[Pinned main A3
log](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45825056341/job/139929272801)
· [v0.34.0 A3
log](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45825056341/job/139929273198)
- On four A5 cards, the same nine-token DeepSeek-V3.2 input produced 4
and 5 local query rows and an Indexer planning charge of 6 on both PCP
ranks. All 15 generated token IDs matched between the baseline and PR
runs on A5. Both A5 runs used the same SwiGLU compatibility path and
produced `abra` where the A3 golden expects `挂`. [A5 output and
rank-layout
comparison](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/22983#issuecomment-7192933891)

#### Full-model Kimi GPQA Diamond accuracy on eight A5 hosts
(2026-11-26)

The full Kimi K3.1 Pro W4A8 MXFP model answered **184/198 questions
correctly (92.93%)** in one GPQA Diamond run on 64 NPUs. All 198
requests completed and yielded a parseable answer. None reached the
output limit.

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Prefill | DP1, TP1, PP4, PCP8, DCP8, MegaMoE mode 2 |
| Decode | DP4, TP8, PP1, PCP1, DCP8 |
| Sampling | Concurrency 60, `max_tokens=131072`, `temperature=1`,
`top_p=0.95`, `reasoning_effort="max"` |
| Speculation | Three DSpark draft tokens, **42.49%** observed
acceptance (694,954 of 1,635,756 proposed tokens) |

The run used #22181, #22333, #22656 and the #22983 deployment snapshot
`192fa3a4`. The Kimi/DSpark production logic exercised by this snapshot
was verified against `c8c30d2b`. The subsequent update to `eef7df15`
changed documentation and code comments only. [Commit
comparison](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/compare/c8c30d2bedcabe5348194a9c42b7d4ff56181c91...eef7df1563e9727807b539a8aca50c239f050925)

An earlier #22181+DCP8 run on the same 198 questions scored **185/198
(93.43%)**. The runs differed by one correct answer. With stochastic
sampling and different serving configurations, this comparison cannot
isolate the accuracy effect of #22983.

#### A5 serving performance at a larger prefill batch budget
(2026-11-26)

Controlled A/B using Kimi K3.1 Pro W4A8 MXFP with one prefill-only
instance on four Ascend A5 hosts (32 NPUs). Both arms ran the same
deployment stack (#22181, #22333 and #22656), with the runtime changes
from #22983 as the only code difference between the arms. Both used
eager execution, DP1/TP1/PP4/PCP8/DCP8, MegaMoE enabled in mode 2, three
DSpark draft tokens, `--max-num-seqs 64`, and 246 registered KV blocks
at each prefill stage. The global `--max-num-batched-tokens` was 24,576.
Each arm completed three cold-start runs with the same warm-up and 120
GSM8K requests, at concurrency 20, targeting 131,072 input tokens and
one output token per request.

| Metric | Baseline without #22983 | Baseline with #22983 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Prefill server mean TTFT | 22.8890 s | **8.6523 s (-62.2%)** |
| Prefill steady-state throughput | 0.8394 req/s | **2.2861 req/s
(+172.3%)** |
| Client throughput over all 120 requests | 0.8206 req/s | **2.1575
req/s (+162.9%)** |
| Mean scheduled tokens per step while requests queued | 24,050 | 24,045
|
| Prefill MegaMoE capacity per rank | 15,800 rows | **4,488 rows** |
| PP3 allocator retries per run, summed over 8 workers | 194 / 192 / 194
| **0 / 0 / 0** |
| PP0 rank 0 sampled HBM, mean / peak | 85.00 / 85.00 GiB | **76.32 /
76.33 GiB** |

Latency and throughput are three-run means. Steady-state throughput uses
the longest continuously backlogged interval between 10% and 90%
completion. Both arms scheduled exactly 1,717,068 tokens per formal run.
HBM was sampled on the same PP0 device for 20 seconds starting about 15
seconds into the load. The per-rank buffer reduction above is a separate
planner estimate. The matched work and disappearance of PP3 allocation
retries are consistent with the smaller MegaMoE reservation restoring
room for transient allocations. The allocation site responsible for the
retries remains unverified.

In a separate single-run budget sweep on the same A5 prefill
configuration with #22983, raising `--max-num-batched-tokens` from
16,384 to 24,576 increased steady-state throughput from **1.958 to 2.259
req/s (+15.4%)** and reduced mean TTFT from **9.968 to 8.643 s
(-13.3%)**, with zero PP3 allocation retries at either budget. At 16,384
in a separate eight-host 1P1D run, keeping both prefill KV pools at 246
blocks gave comparable client latency and throughput and zero PP3
retries with or without #22983. Increasing the prefill KV pool to 1,129
blocks in a separate 16,384-token 1P1D run with #22983 brought back 192
PP3 allocation retries. The measured benefit at 24,576 applies to the
fixed-KV prefill-only configuration above.

#### A5 throughput at a 10-second prefill TTFT target

On the same A5 prefill-only setup with #22983 and a 24,576-token batch
budget, concurrency 23 sustained **2.2887 requests/s (about 2.3)** at
**9.831 s mean server-side TTFT**. All three runs met the 10-second mean
TTFT target (9.813–9.841 s), and two reached **2.2998 requests/s**.

| Concurrency | Runs within 10 s mean TTFT | Mean server-side TTFT |
Mean prefill steady-state QPS |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 20 | 3/3 | 8.652 s | 2.2861 |
| 23 | 3/3 | 9.831 s | 2.2887 |
| 24 | 0/2 | 10.216 s | 2.2998 |

At concurrency 20, two runs also reached 2.2998 requests/s, with mean
TTFT of 8.660 s and 8.654 s. Mean steady-state throughput was already
close to 2.3 requests/s at concurrency 20.

[BugFix] Fix prefill crash for KV-sharing consumer layers (Gemma-4) (#23008)

## What this PR does / why we need it?
Fixes #21972
Gemma-4 uses YOCO-style KV sharing: layers marked `is_kv_shared_layer`
have no `k_proj`/`v_proj` and call attention as `attn(q, None, None)`.
They produce no K/V of their own and can only read the KV cache written
by their producer layer.

The Ascend `PrefillNoCache` path is a dense-KV bypass: `_get_fia_params`
returns `key`/`value` unchanged with `block_table=None`, and the caller
then trims the dense K/V via `key = key[:num_tokens]`. For a consumer
layer `key` is `None`, so any model with KV sharing (currently Gemma-4
and the Gemma-4 MTP drafter) crashes during prefill with:

```
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
```

at `forward_fused_infer_attention` -> `key = key[:num_tokens]`.

This PR makes the backend recognize a KV-sharing consumer (`key is
None`): `_get_fia_params` requires the paged cache view instead of the
dense bypass, the dense K/V trimming is skipped, and
`is_prefill_no_cache` is passed as `False` to `DeviceOperator` so the
consumer is handled as paged KV on the large-head prefill path. The C8
path also initializes the producer cache handle, because the consumer
layer skips `_reshape_and_cache`.

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Gemma-4 (including the MTP drafter) previously failed during
prefill on Ascend NPU; it now runs.

## How was this patch tested?

Hardware: A3 (single die, `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`),
`enforce_eager=True`, `gemma-4-E4B-it` with `gemma-4-E4B-it-assistant`.
Baseline (no speculative decoding) and MTP (`method=mtp`,
`num_speculative_tokens=2`) both complete and shut down cleanly.
`llm.chat` on three prompts returns identical, correct results for both
runs: `Paris` / `391` / `Jupiter` (3/3 match). Before the fix, the same
script deterministically raised the `TypeError` above in
`forward_fused_infer_attention`.

Existing e2e coverage does not reach this path: the 31B target has
`num_kv_shared_layers=0`, and the 31B drafter's prefill state is
rewritten to `PrefillCacheHit` by the Gemma-4 speculator, so
`test_gemma4_mtp_spec_decode_model_runner_v2` would not catch a
regression here. The only configuration that runs a consumer layer in
`PrefillNoCache` is the E4B target (18/42 shared layers), which is what
the manual test above uses. A new unit test
(`test_kv_sharing_consumer_prefill_reads_producer_cache`) covers this
combination directly: a consumer layer in `PrefillNoCache` must return
the producer cache view, a non-`None` block table, and `seq_lens_list`
as the KV lengths.

Graph mode: with `cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY` the baseline run
completes and shuts down cleanly. The MTP run fails only during FULL
graph capture with `aclnnFusedInferAttentionScoreV3 ... 561002` (`When D
is 512, inputlayout TND q_rope and k_rope should not be null`), raised
from `_npu_fused_infer_attention_score_get_max_workspace` while
capturing the draft model. This is the pre-existing Gemma-4 512-dim TND
limitation tracked in #19559, not caused by this change: the FIA call
path never passes `q_rope`/`k_rope` regardless of KV sharing. With
`cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`, MTP completes and returns correct answers
(`The capital of France is Paris`, `The largest planet in the solar
system is Jupiter`; the arithmetic prompt was cut off by `max_tokens=16`
before producing the number).

Unit tests: `pytest tests/ut/attention/test_attention_v1.py -k
kv_sharing` -> 3 passed, 45 deselected. AI assistance was used to
prepare this change; the diff and the test runs above were reviewed
manually.

[Feature][KV Pool] Support DeepSeek-V4 layerwise KV offload (#22024)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable DeepSeek-V4 Flash and Pro to reuse shared HBM buffers on the
Prefill side with the layerwise KV offload framework from #21256.
Layerwise reuse lowers the HBM footprint per global KV block so the same
Prefill KV budget can hold more blocks.

Reuse covers the target model's C4 and C128 compressed history, indexer
history, sliding-window KV, and compressor states. The save path keeps
the public prefix pages selected by the coordinator and adds the live
window needed for the next chunk. Chunk continuation restores the live
window. SWA-only layers use the registered SWA cache name for Mooncake
Push. Shared buffers wait for Store saves and relevant P-to-D sends
before reuse, using the transfer dependency introduced in #21891.

### User-visible changes

Shared buffers require the top-level role to be `kv_producer`. Prefill
combines `AscendStoreConnector` and `MooncakePushConnector` through
`MultiConnector`. The P/D proxy caps Prefill requests at one generated
token. Decode uses resident HBM caches and the MTP draft cache stays
resident. Combining shared-buffer reuse with DSpark is deferred.

Set these options on the Prefill AscendStore child connector. This
example keeps layers 0 and 1 resident. Set the independent layer list to
`[]` to allow the first two SWA layers to participate in reuse. Omit
`layerwise_num_shared_buffers` for regular layerwise pooling.

```json
{
  "backend": "memcache",
  "use_layerwise": true,
  "layerwise_num_shared_buffers": 3,
  "layerwise_prefetch_layers": 4,
  "layerwise_independent_layers": [0, 1]
}
```

### How was this patch tested?

#### CPU unit test coverage

- Flash and Pro cache planning, producer-only role validation, and MTP
draft-cache residency.
- SWA checkpoint saves and chunk-continuation loads, private GVA
snapshot fallback, and PCP publication ordering.
- SWA-only Mooncake Push dispatch, connector dependencies, and Qwen4Exp
layerwise cache reuse regression coverage.

#### Single-host 950PR P/D functional test

The archived run used DeepSeek-V4 Flash with P TP4 and D TP4,
PP=DP=PCP=DCP=1, EP, Model Runner V2, PIECEWISE graphs, FP8 target and
indexer KV, and one MTP draft token. Prefill used Memcache with three
shared buffers, prefetch depth 2, and no independent layers. Decode used
resident HBM. Local HBM prefix caching was disabled on both sides. The
Prefill chunk was 1,024 tokens, the maximum model length was 4,096, and
GPU memory utilization was 0.86. The tested snapshot was `a64a61c6b`
with #21262 and its integration changes applied.

| Completed requests | Input tokens per request | Output tokens per
request | KV tokens received by Decode | Decode MTP draft tokens |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 3/3 | 2,067 | 64 | 6,198 | 104 proposed, 91 accepted, 13 rejected |

The first two SWA layers participated in reuse. Decode set the KV load
failure policy to `fail` and computed a total of three prompt tokens
locally. These are request-level results.

#### Two-host 950DT P/D performance

The archived Flash benchmark used `09adb5d33` with #21262 and the
integration changes used at the time. Prefill and Decode each ran on one
A5 950DT host at TP8 with PP=DP=PCP=DCP=1. Both used EP, Model Runner
V2, PIECEWISE graphs, FP8 target and indexer KV, and one MTP draft
token. Both used automatic KV sizing with `gpu_memory_utilization=0.90`
and a maximum model length of 132,096. Prefill used 8,192 or 16,384
batched tokens and Decode used 2,048. Memcache used `device_urma`, and
all groups used Mooncake Push for P-to-D transfer.

AISBench sent 128 requests per group through the same P/D proxy at
concurrency 32. Each request had 131,072 input tokens and generated one
token. The repeat rate was 0.9, with seed 1023 and either 1 or 32
prefixes. Prefill and Decode profiling ran separately from timing. All
rows completed 128/128 requests. The 16K B32 row uses the complete
rerun.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark configurations and reproduction parameters</summary>

| Case | Prefill prefix source | Prefill connectors and prefix settings
| Shared-buffer reuse |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | Single prefix, HBM only | Mooncake Push with local prefix caching
enabled | Off |
| B1/B32 | Single/32 prefixes, DRAM only | Memcache layerwise pooling +
Mooncake Push with local prefix caching disabled | Off |
| C1/C32 | Single/32 prefixes, DRAM only | Same pool mode as the
corresponding B case | Three shared buffers, prefetch depth 4, layers 0
and 1 resident |

Decode used the Mooncake Push consumer and resident HBM in every group.

- #23107 starts layerwise KV prefetch earlier and has merged.
- #21262 batches load metadata queries and lease acquisition across
cache groups.
- #22784 sizes GVA allocations using each cache group's payload.

#### Prefill KV block capacity

The following capacity figures come from the B32 and C32 runs in the
performance table. Both used 32 prefixes, the same source snapshot
within each chunk size, and automatic KV sizing. B32 used Memcache
layerwise pooling without shared buffers. C32 used three shared buffers,
prefetch depth 4, and layers 0 and 1 resident. The global block count
comes from the Prefill `vllm:cache_config_info.num_gpu_blocks` metric.

+    a5 = cache_format != "a3"
+    packed = cache_format == "a5_packed"
+    main_dim = 608 if packed else 512
+    main_dtype = torch.float8_e4m3fn if packed else torch.bfloat16
+    large = block_size * (608 if packed else 1024)
+    small = block_size * (132 if a5 else 130)
+    specs = {}
+    for layer, ratio in enumerate(ratios):
+        prefix = f"model.layers.{layer}.self_attn"
+        if ratio > 1:
+            state_rows = block_size // (16 if ratio == 4 else (8 if a5 else 4))

+                    block_size=state_rows,
+                    num_kv_heads=1,
+                    head_size=512,
+                    dtype=torch.float32,
+                    sliding_window=8,
+                    page_size_padded=small,
+                )
+        specs[prefix + ".swa_cache"] = AscendSlidingWindowMLASpec(
+            block_size=block_size,
+            num_kv_heads=1,
+            head_size=main_dim,
+            dtype=main_dtype,
+            sliding_window=128,
+            model_version="deepseek_v4",

+        if ratio > 1:
+            specs[prefix + ".attn"] = AscendMLAAttentionSpec(

+                tokens_per_state=ratio,
+                num_kv_heads=1,
+                head_size=main_dim,
+                dtype=main_dtype,
+                model_version="deepseek_v4",

+        runtime.speculative_config = SimpleNamespace(method="mtp", num_speculative_tokens=1, use_eagle=lambda: True)
+        runtime.num_hash_lookahead_tokens = 0
+        specs["mtp.layers.0.self_attn.swa_cache"] = replace(specs["model.layers.0.self_attn.swa_cache"], is_draft=True)

[Performance][KV Transfer] Optimize Mooncake V2 addresses and SWA metadata (#22661)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Long-context Mooncake V2 transfers spend CPU time building per-block
Python objects and repeating address arithmetic across layers. Pull
metadata also carries SWA block IDs outside the retained window.

This PR:

- Represents block transfer ranges as NumPy arrays and builds singleton
or contiguous ranges only when the layout needs them. Reuses
request-scoped byte offsets and length lists across matching pull
layouts within a spec/remote bucket, with scalar arithmetic for a single
range.
- Vectorizes Push descriptor arithmetic and reuses request-ordered block
arrays across cache components.
- Trims Pull SWA metadata to the retained suffix after speculative-block
trimming. Retention includes `extra_retained_tokens`, the largest
combined window in a uniform group, and an unaligned boundary page. The
receiver recovers the suffix's logical start before intersecting it with
the consumer's unhashed blocks, preserving prefix-hit and block-scale
mapping.

NumPy/address caching and SWA trimming are separate commits. READ/WRITE
still receive Python integer lists; no Mooncake array API or dependency
upgrade is required. Existing byte-contiguity rules, descriptor order,
partial-head offsets, independent P/D strides, and completion/failure
handling are preserved. Mamba keeps its separate address path.

Inspired by the vectorized descriptor approach in
vllm-project/vllm#62478. This PR is independent of #20903 (per-request
submission and pool configuration).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

**CPU correctness on ARM in the A3 runtime (before rebase):**

- 445 pull-worker and push-sending tests passed for the NumPy/cache
commit.
- 603 pull-worker, scheduler, SWA-handoff and virtual-pull tests passed
for the final SWA commit, including three retention cases covering extra
retained tokens across page boundaries and different retention windows
within a group.
- Address coverage includes empty/singleton and fragmented inputs,
padded and partial-head layouts, independent strides, high addresses,
descriptor ordering, and reuse of computed address components.
- Tests imported the candidate Mooncake Python package through an
isolated source overlay. These CPU tests do not exercise native
transport or prove NPU numerical accuracy.

**Full P/D serving on ARM/Ascend:**

Both runs used the pre-rebase `631d988` source, with imported module
paths and hashes checked. Warmup was excluded from the reported
benchmark windows. Baselines below are historical runs using the
corresponding workload/configuration, not alternating concurrent A/B
experiments.

| A5: 8 x Ascend 950DT, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 | Earlier V2 with SWA
trimming | Hybrid | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Mean TTFT (s) | 45.000 | 40.215 | 39.390 |
| P99 TTFT (s) | 91.766 | 97.990 | 95.014 |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 17.9 | 16.3 | 15.9 |
| Mean ITL (ms) | 111.2 | 102.8 | 103.4 |
| Output throughput (token/s) | 11312.957 | 12538.458 | 12785.476 |

A5 configuration: P/D each DP4/TP1/PCP1/EP4; KV/indexer FP8; DSpark5
with actual acceptance; 16 proxy workers; 3,200 requests at concurrency
800, each with 131,155 input tokens and 1,024 output tokens. P used
eager execution; D used async scheduling and FULL_DECODE_ONLY, with
prefix caching disabled. vLLM
`62d4bc3c7e33b1b6c906e233e6af2d3506c482ca`, Ascend image base
`7dcdb690caf879a17ab07382880d5773f5202e20`, torch 2.10.0+cpu and
torch_npu 2.10.0.post7. All 3,200 requests completed successfully. Mean
TTFT was 12.47% lower and throughput 13.02% higher than the earlier V2
baseline. Relative to Hybrid, TTFT was 2.05% lower and throughput 1.97%
higher; a single historical comparison does not establish a stable 2%
advantage. P99 TTFT was higher than the earlier V2 baseline, and mean
ITL slightly higher than Hybrid.

| A3: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 | Hybrid | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Mean TTFT (s) | 3.204 | 3.327 |
| P99 TTFT (s) | 9.488 | 9.701 |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 33.323 | 33.439 |
| Output throughput (token/s) | 10575.552 | 10537.377 |

A3 configuration: P/D each DP8/TP1/EP8; 16 proxy workers; 1,600 requests
at concurrency 400, 65,538 input tokens and 1,000 output tokens, with
65,536-token D prefix hits. DSpark used synthetic acceptance length 4,
so this is not an actual-acceptance accuracy test. All 1,600 requests
completed successfully without request retries. Throughput was within
0.36% of historical Hybrid; mean TTFT remained 3.86% higher.

These serving runs validate performance and request completion for the
stated cases, not independent numerical parity or every layout/topology.
End-to-end differences cannot be attributed entirely to address
construction. Push performance and NPU numerical parity remain
unmeasured; required CI remains pending.

**Local repository checks on the submitted commit:** Ruff check/format,
spelling, C++ formatting, Markdown, PNG,
filename/package/import/context-manager hooks, and `git diff --check`
passed. Actionlint environment installation stalled on Windows;
actionlint, gitleaks and shellcheck remain for CI. The
logger/long-function/symbolic-meta hook launchers encountered Windows
`/bin/bash` or `python3` path issues. Equivalent native-Python logger
scanning, the long-function checker applied to added PR lines, and the
native-Python symbolic-meta check passed separately.

**Rebase validation (2026-11-26):** Rebased onto upstream
`5e4e3a22f1a95bcd6d61d0389bb390067899076a`; the rebase produced
`f1d22fd5b`. The only textual conflict was the pull-worker utility
import: preserve upstream's `worker_rank_to_dcp_rank` while removing the
obsolete grouping import. Upstream's version-dependent DCP routing fix
is retained in both Pull and Push. AST comparisons confirm the
address-optimization and SWA methods are unchanged. Sixty
source-isolated CPU checks passed for the rank helper and Pull grouping
across both ordering modes and TP/PCP/DCP combinations. Supported
repository hooks and `git diff --check` passed. NPU
serving/accuracy/performance were not rerun after rebase; the ARM and
serving results above belong to the pre-rebase revision.

**Test simplification (`7d4c0428c`):** Consolidated overlapping Pull
cache tests into the existing cross-layer range-reuse test and reduced
the SWA Cartesian matrix to six explicit boundary cases, including extra
retention across a page boundary. This removes 76 test lines and eight
cases while retaining request/call isolation, independent strides,
different transfer lengths, and suffix/prefix-hit coverage. The two
release-note YAML fragments were removed; production code is unchanged.
After rebase and simplification, 610 tests passed on the ARM A5 runtime
across `test_pull_worker.py`, `test_pull_scheduler.py`,
`test_push_sending.py`, `test_swa_handoff.py`, and
`test_virtual_pull.py`, using an isolated source overlay with hashes
checked. Supported repository hooks and `git diff --check` passed. No
model services or NPU workload were started.

AI assistance was used for implementation and validation.

### Checklist

- [x] Address-generation and retained-window regression tests
- [x] ARM CPU runtime tests
- [x] A3 and A5 full P/D serving performance measurements
- [ ] Independent NPU numerical parity
- [ ] Required CI checks

[Doc] Update DeepSeek V4.1 Flash A3 PD and Memcache guides (#22727)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Update the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash guide to align the A3 deployment examples
in sections 5.2 (1P1D PD) and 5.3 (Memcache KV Cache Pool), and document
an LM head tuning configuration in section 9.

- Embed the current official
`examples/external_online_dp/launch_online_dp.py` script in A3 section
5.2.1.1. Document its PP and template-path options and nine positional
arguments; the A3 deployment retains PP=1.
- Use W4A8 weights, Prefill DP4/PCP4/TP1 with EPLB, Decode DP16/TP1,
fastokens, and four proxy workers.
- Configure Prefill EPLB with the `stair` policy and 16 redundant
experts. Explain all four `--eplb-config` parameters and distinguish
short benchmarks (`window_size: 64`, `step_interval: 128`) from
production (`1000`, `3000`).
- Set `enable_fused_mc2: 3` on both roles. Prefill enables
`enable_shared_expert_dp`; Decode uses a 432-token budget and 72
sequences, with graph execution and recompute scheduling.
- Update the Memcache role scripts to use launcher arguments `$2`
through `$8`, retain `MultiConnector` with `MooncakeConnectorV2` and
`AscendStoreConnector`, and configure Memcache `use_layerwise` as `true`
on Prefill and `false` on Decode. Remove the contradictory blanket
prohibition from the Memcache instructions.
- Keep network, model, and Memcache paths together at the top of each
Memcache role script. Enable `VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1` on both roles and
configure the Memcache library directory, existing library paths, and
`/usr/local/lib/` in a single `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` export. Keep the
Memcache-specific exports inside each role script and remove the
strict-shell and locked-memory prerequisites from these A3 examples.
- Document four-way LM head tensor parallelism for peak-performance
benchmarking on the A3 Decode node: merge
`finegrained_tp_config.lmhead_tensor_parallel_size: 4` into the existing
`--additional-config`, and use `--max-num-seqs 24` with
`--max-num-batched-tokens 168`. Link to the fine-grained TP guide.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Documentation only; runtime defaults and APIs are unchanged. This
updates existing deployment scenarios and introduces no new
configuration options. No release note fragment is required.

No runtime tests were added for this documentation-only change.

0.45.0, codespell, and typos passed.
- Verified that the embedded A3 launcher exactly matches the official

unchanged by this launcher update.
- In section 5.3.2, all four shell blocks passed `bash -n`, the Python

- Verified that section 5.4 exactly matches the PR base and that the

- Parsed the section 9 JSON and checked its shell fragment with `bash

- A fresh English `bash tools/rtd_build.sh` build with `--strict`

[Feature][Model] Adopt fused MsaIndexScore TopK with forced-block support (#23122)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

MiniMax-M3's fused index-score Top-K
(`cann_ops_transformer.msa_index_score`
with `return_choice`) was gated behind a new hardware capability,
`HardwareCapability.MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_SCORE_TOPK_FUSION`, and therefore
enabled
on A5 only. A2, A3 and A5 all run the same CANN operator, and A2/A3
behave
identically, so this capability gate carried no real information. It
only made
A2/A3 run a separate score pass, Top-K and sort on every index-score
step.

This PR removes the hardware gate. The fused path is now decided solely
by
whether the installed CANN package provides the fused output:

- `vllm_ascend/models/minimax_m3/ops/msa_m3_npu.py`:
  `_can_use_index_score_topk_fusion()` no longer calls

`get_current_hardware_profile().supports(MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_SCORE_TOPK_FUSION)`.
The two real constraints stay: `0 < topk <= 128` with `topk % 8 == 0`
(the
operator's non-aligned write-back returns uninitialised memory for
multi-token
  requests), and the `_index_score_has_return_choice()` signature probe.
  Docstrings are updated to match.
- `vllm_ascend/device/hardware_profile.py`: removes the
`HardwareCapability.MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_SCORE_TOPK_FUSION` enum member with
its
comment, and its registration in the A5 profile. No references remain
anywhere
  in the tree.

Behavior:
- A3 (and A2, when the same CANN package is installed): prefill and
sorted
decode with an aligned `topk` now take the fused path and skip the
separate
  `_minimax_m3_index_score` plus `_minimax_m3_index_prefill_topk` /
  `index_decode_topk_fused` calls.
- A5: unchanged.
- A CANN package without `return_choice`: still falls back to the
separate path.
- An unaligned `topk`: still falls back to the separate path.

Fixes # (add the related issue if one exists)

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. No configuration key, environment variable, API or default switch is
added
or changed. `MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_SCORE_TOPK_FUSION` is an internal
`HardwareCapability` enum member and was never exposed to users. The
only
observable difference is index-score path performance for MiniMax-M3 on
A2/A3;
the computed indices are unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit tests, run on this revision (`main` + this PR) in the `pxt_test_v2`
container:

```bash
pytest tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_msa_m3.py -q
# 626 passed
```

The cases touched by this PR:

```bash
pytest tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_msa_m3.py \
  -q -k "fusion or fused or a2_a3 or index_score"
# 44 passed, 582 deselected

pytest "tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_msa_m3.py::test_topk_fusion_is_enabled_on_a2_a3_and_a5" \
       "tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_msa_m3.py::test_ascendc_index_prefill_uses_fused_topk_on_a2_a3" -v
# test_topk_fusion_is_enabled_on_a2_a3_and_a5             PASSED
# test_ascendc_index_prefill_uses_fused_topk_on_a2_a3[a2] PASSED
# test_ascendc_index_prefill_uses_fused_topk_on_a2_a3[a3] PASSED
```

Test changes:
- `test_topk_fusion_is_enabled_on_a5_only` becomes
`test_topk_fusion_is_enabled_on_a2_a3_and_a5`: A5, A3 and A2 all assert
  `True`, where A3 and A2 previously asserted `False`.
- New parameterized fixture `fused_index_ops_a2_a3` (`a2` / `a3`) and
new
`test_ascendc_index_prefill_uses_fused_topk_on_a2_a3`, which asserts
that an
aligned `topk` on A2/A3 calls `msa_index_score(return_choice=1, topk=16,
local_blocks=1)` directly and that neither the separate score path nor
the
  separate Top-K path is called.
- The two cases that previously relied on "A3 is unsupported, so fall
back" now
cover `_index_score_has_return_choice` returning `False`, which is the
actual
  condition for falling back to the separate path.
- The operator signature/import probe tests no longer patch
  `get_current_hardware_profile`, which had become inert.
- `tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py`: drops
`MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_SCORE_TOPK_FUSION` from the expected A5 capability
set.

Note: the container baseline (`main@405617bae`) has a pre-existing
circular
import (`device_op.py` -> `vllm_ascend.ops` -> `device_op`) that
reproduces on
the pristine tree and is unrelated to this PR. Tests were run with a
local
pytest plugin that imports `vllm_ascend.ops` first; the plugin is not
part of
this PR.

Not covered: end-to-end accuracy and performance runs. Numerical
equivalence
between the fused path and the separate score + Top-K + sort path
(including the
per-token `local_blocks` difference on multi-token requests) was
validated on A5
earlier; A2/A3 reuse the same CANN operator and the same gate
conditions.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

Checklist notes:
- **Boundary**: the `topk` bounds are still enforced by `0 < topk <=
128` and
`topk % 8 == 0`, covered by `test_fusion_gate_rejects_unsupported_k` (0,
129),
  `test_fusion_gate_rejects_unaligned_topk` (1, 2, 4, 12, 17, 127) and
`test_fusion_gate_allows_aligned_topk` (8, 16, 24, 32, 128). All still
pass.
- **Regression**: this is not a bugfix, so it does not apply.
- **Error path**: `test_topk_fusion_requires_the_new_operator` and
`test_topk_fusion_is_off_when_the_operator_is_unimportable` cover a CANN
package missing `return_choice` and a `cann_ops_transformer` that cannot
be
  imported at all.
- **Performance**: this PR touches a performance-sensitive path
(index-score
  runs every step), but no benchmark is attached, so the item is left
  unchecked.

[BugFix][Upstream] Tolerate a missing backend attribute in GroupCoordinator destroy (#22192)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`GroupCoordinatorPatch.destroy()` in
`vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_distributed.py`
reads `self.backend` to decide whether the device process group is owned
by the
HCCL registry (backend `hccl`) or has to be destroyed directly:

```python
device_group = getattr(self, "device_group", None)
if device_group is not None and self.backend != "hccl":
    torch.distributed.destroy_process_group(device_group)
```

`backend` is only assigned in `GroupCoordinatorPatch.__init__`. The
upstream
vLLM test
`tests/distributed/test_flashinfer_pcie_ipc_all_reduce.py::test_group_destroy_releases_communicator_before_process_groups`
builds a coordinator with `GroupCoordinator.__new__(GroupCoordinator)`,
so
`backend` is never set. With the vllm-ascend patch installed, the call
fails
before the test can assert the destroy order:

```
AttributeError: 'GroupCoordinatorPatch' object has no attribute 'backend'
vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_distributed.py:227: in destroy
```

This is the failure reported in #21966 (weekly `upstream-test` shard).

This PR reads the backend with `getattr` and treats a missing value as
"not hccl", so the device group is destroyed directly. That matches the
upstream `GroupCoordinator.destroy()`, which always destroys the device
group,
and it keeps the NPU production path unchanged: the Ascend backend is
always
`hccl`, so the device group stays owned by the registry and is released
by
`_release_hccl_resources()` as before.

Fixes #21966

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No behaviour change for a running engine: the Ascend backend is always
`hccl`,
so the production destroy path is bit-for-bit the same. The change only
removes
the `AttributeError` on a destroy path that previously crashed, which
also fixes
the upstream vLLM test suite when the vllm-ascend patch is installed. A
release
note fragment is included (`release_notes/fragments/22192.yaml`).

### How was this patch tested?

#### CPU unit test (new)

- Regression test:

`tests/ut/patch/worker/patch_common/test_patch_distributed.py::test_destroy_without_backend_attribute_releases_groups_in_order`
It builds a `GroupCoordinatorPatch` through `__new__` (so `backend` is
never
assigned), attaches a fake device communicator plus a device and a CPU
process
group, and asserts that `destroy()` releases the communicator before the
two
process groups - the same order the upstream test requires. Without this
  change the test fails with
`AttributeError: 'GroupCoordinatorPatch' object has no attribute
'backend'`
  at `vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_distributed.py:227`.
- Local CPU run of the whole module: **18 passed**
(`python -m pytest
tests/ut/patch/worker/patch_common/test_patch_distributed.py -q`).

#### Upstream vLLM test (the one #21966 is about)

The upstream test was run directly with the vllm-ascend patch applied
(`adapt_patch()`), against vLLM
`vllm@c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15`:

| | result |
|---|---|
| without this fix | **FAILED** - `AttributeError:
'GroupCoordinatorPatch' object has no attribute 'backend'` at
`patch_distributed.py:227` |
| with this fix | **PASSED** |

#### Real-NPU validation (new)

`tests/manual/test_group_coordinator_destroy_npu.py` validates on real
Ascend
hardware that the production path really is unchanged, instead of only
asserting it. It was run on **2 x Ascend 910B3** (torch_npu
2.10.0.post4,
CANN 9.1.0, vLLM v0.33.0):

```
torchrun --nproc_per_node=2 tests/manual/test_group_coordinator_destroy_npu.py
```

The script creates a **real** HCCL process group, runs a collective over
it,
and checks that `destroy()` releases the device group **exactly once
through the
HCCL registry** while the gloo cpu group is destroyed directly, that the
registry holds no dangling entry afterwards, and that a fresh HCCL group
can
still be created and used on the same devices afterwards.

Differential result on the same hardware:

| check | pre-fix | with this fix |
|---|---|---|
| coordinator backend is `hccl` on Ascend | PASS | PASS |
| real HCCL device group was created | PASS | PASS |
| `all_reduce` over the real HCCL group works (got 2.0) | PASS | PASS |
| coordinator acquired an HCCL registry key | PASS | PASS |
| hccl device group destroyed exactly once (by the registry) | PASS |
PASS |
| `destroy()` destroyed exactly the device group and the cpu group |
PASS | PASS |
| gloo cpu group destroyed directly | PASS | PASS |
| `device_group` / `cpu_group` attributes deleted | PASS | PASS |
| coordinator holds no HCCL registry key after `destroy()` | PASS | PASS
|
| a fresh HCCL group can be created after `destroy()` | PASS | PASS |
| `all_reduce` works on the fresh group | PASS | PASS |
| orphan coordinator (no `backend` attribute) is destroyable |
**AttributeError** | PASS |
| orphan coordinator destroyed its device group directly | (not reached)
| PASS |
| script exit code | 1 | **0** |

So every NPU-path check behaves identically before and after the change,
and
the only difference is the previously crashing case.

The device group is destroyed exactly once in both cases because the
HCCL
registry's `release()` itself calls
`torch.distributed.destroy_process_group`.
The check therefore counts the destroy calls rather than just asserting
the
group was not destroyed directly, which would not have distinguished the
two
code paths.

#### Other checks

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed files: passed.
- Repository pre-commit hooks (`check_python_src_init`,
`check_forbidden_imports`,
`check_boolean_context_manager`, `check_long_functions`,
`check_logger`): passed.
- `codespell` on the changed files: passed.

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: the regression test covers a
coordinator that never went through `__init__`, i.e. the only case in
which
  `backend` is missing. The existing tests keep covering the `hccl` and
  non-`hccl` backends.
- [x] **Regression test**:
`test_destroy_without_backend_attribute_releases_groups_in_order` fails
  without this fix.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: the test drives the `destroy()`
path
  that previously raised `AttributeError`.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: the test asserts the real destroy
order
(communicator before the process groups it depends on), not internal
state.
The NPU script additionally exercises a real HCCL group with a
collective,
  not a mock.
- [x] **Performance impact**: the change only replaces an attribute
lookup with
a `getattr` on the group teardown path, which runs once per process
group at
  shutdown.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""Real-NPU validation for the GroupCoordinatorPatch.destroy() HCCL path.
+
+This is the NPU counterpart of the CPU unit test in
+``tests/ut/patch/worker/patch_common/test_patch_distributed.py``.
+
+It validates, on real Ascend hardware, that the ``destroy()`` path of
+``GroupCoordinatorPatch`` behaves identically with and without the
+``getattr(self, "backend", None)`` fallback introduced for issue #21966:
+
+* On Ascend the backend is always ``hccl``, so the device process group must
+  be released through the HCCL registry (``_release_hccl_resources()``), and
+  the ``backend != "hccl"`` branch must not destroy it a second time.
+* The gloo CPU group is destroyed directly.
+* After ``destroy()`` the registry holds no dangling entry, and a fresh HCCL
+  group can be created and used on the same devices.
+* A coordinator built without ``__init__`` (the upstream-test shape, so no
+  ``backend`` attribute) is still destroyable, and destroys its device group
+  directly.
+
+The two ranks run in spawned processes, so the test needs two NPU devices::
+
+    pytest -sv tests/e2e/pull_request/two_card/test_group_coordinator_destroy_npu.py
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+import torch.multiprocessing as mp
+import torch_npu  # noqa: F401  (registers the npu backend)
+from vllm.utils.network_utils import get_open_port
+
+from vllm_ascend.patch.worker.patch_distributed import GroupCoordinatorPatch
+
+_WORLD_SIZE = 2
+
+
+def _check(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
+    rank = os.environ.get("RANK", "?")
+    if condition:
+        print(f"[rank{rank}] PASS: {message}", flush=True)
+    else:
+        print(f"[rank{rank}] FAIL: {message}", flush=True)
+        raise AssertionError(message)
+
+
+def _validate_real_hccl_coordinator(world_size: int, local_rank: int) -> None:
+    """The normal Ascend path: backend is hccl, the registry owns the group."""
+    coordinator = GroupCoordinatorPatch(
+        group_ranks=[list(range(world_size))],
+        local_rank=local_rank,
+        torch_distributed_backend="hccl",
+        use_device_communicator=False,
+        group_name="npu_destroy_validation",
+    )
+
+    _check(coordinator.backend == "hccl", "coordinator backend is 'hccl' on Ascend")
+    _check(coordinator.device_group is not None, "real HCCL device group was created")
+
+    # Capture the handles before destroy() deletes the attributes.
+    device_group = coordinator.device_group
+    cpu_group = coordinator.cpu_group
+
+    # The collective proves the group is genuinely functional, not just created.
+    tensor = torch.ones(4, device=f"npu:{local_rank}")
+    dist.all_reduce(tensor, group=device_group)
+    torch.npu.synchronize()
+    _check(
+        bool((tensor == world_size).all().item()),
+        f"all_reduce over the real HCCL group works (got {tensor[0].item()})",
+    )
+
+    _check(
+        len(getattr(coordinator, "_acquired_hccl_keys", [])) > 0,
+        "coordinator acquired an HCCL registry key",
+    )
+
+    # Count the destroy_process_group calls. The HCCL registry's release()
+    # also calls torch.distributed.destroy_process_group, so the call count
+    # alone does not separate the two paths. What does: on Ascend the device
+    # group must be destroyed exactly once (by the registry), and the cpu
+    # group exactly once (directly). A second direct destroy of the device
+    # group would show up as a count of 2.
+    destroy_calls: list[object] = []
+    real_destroy = dist.destroy_process_group
+
+    def spy_destroy(group=None, *args, **kwargs):
+        destroy_calls.append(group)
+        return real_destroy(group, *args, **kwargs)
+
+    dist.destroy_process_group = spy_destroy
+    try:
+        coordinator.destroy()
+    finally:
+        dist.destroy_process_group = real_destroy
+
+    device_group_destroy_count = sum(1 for group in destroy_calls if group is device_group)
+    _check(
+        device_group_destroy_count == 1,
+        "hccl device group was destroyed exactly once (by the registry)",
+    )
+    _check(
+        len(destroy_calls) == 2,
+        f"destroy() destroyed exactly the device group and the cpu group (calls={len(destroy_calls)})",
+    )
+    _check(cpu_group in destroy_calls, "gloo cpu group was destroyed directly")
+
+    _check(not hasattr(coordinator, "device_group"), "device_group attribute was deleted")
+    _check(not hasattr(coordinator, "cpu_group"), "cpu_group attribute was deleted")
+    _check(
+        len(getattr(coordinator, "_acquired_hccl_keys", [])) == 0,
+        "coordinator holds no HCCL registry key after destroy()",
+    )
+
+    # A fresh group must still work, i.e. destroy() left the HCCL domain
+    # in a usable state.
+    second = GroupCoordinatorPatch(
+        group_ranks=[list(range(world_size))],
+        local_rank=local_rank,
+        torch_distributed_backend="hccl",
+        use_device_communicator=False,
+        group_name="npu_destroy_validation_second",
+    )
+    _check(second.device_group is not None, "a fresh HCCL group can be created after destroy()")
+
+    tensor2 = torch.ones(4, device=f"npu:{local_rank}")
+    dist.all_reduce(tensor2, group=second.device_group)
+    torch.npu.synchronize()
+    _check(
+        bool((tensor2 == world_size).all().item()),
+        "all_reduce works on the fresh group after the first destroy()",
+    )
+    second.destroy()
+
+
+def _validate_coordinator_without_backend(world_size: int) -> None:
+    """The upstream shape: no ``backend`` attribute, so destroy() must not raise."""
+    orphan = GroupCoordinatorPatch.__new__(GroupCoordinatorPatch)
+    _check(
+        not hasattr(orphan, "backend"),
+        "orphan coordinator has no 'backend' attribute (upstream shape)",
+    )
+
+    orphan_device_group = dist.new_group(list(range(world_size)), backend="hccl")
+    orphan_cpu_group = dist.new_group(list(range(world_size)), backend="gloo")
+    orphan.device_group = orphan_device_group
+    orphan.cpu_group = orphan_cpu_group
+    orphan.mq_broadcaster = None
+
+    destroy_calls: list[object] = []
+    real_destroy = dist.destroy_process_group
+
+    def spy_destroy(group=None, *args, **kwargs):
+        destroy_calls.append(group)
+        return real_destroy(group, *args, **kwargs)
+
+    dist.destroy_process_group = spy_destroy
+    try:
+        orphan.destroy()
+    finally:
+        dist.destroy_process_group = real_destroy
+
+    _check(not hasattr(orphan, "device_group"), "orphan released its device_group attribute")
+    _check(not hasattr(orphan, "cpu_group"), "orphan released its cpu_group attribute")
+    _check(
+        orphan_device_group in destroy_calls,
+        "orphan coordinator destroyed its device group directly",
+    )
+    _check(
+        orphan_cpu_group in destroy_calls,
+        "orphan coordinator destroyed its cpu group directly",
+    )
+
+
+def _worker(rank: int, port: int) -> None:
+    """One of the two ranks: validate the destroy path on a real HCCL group."""
+    # The same environment a torchrun launch provides, so the HCCL backend
+    # uses the usual rendezvous.
+    os.environ["MASTER_ADDR"] = "127.0.0.1"
+    os.environ["MASTER_PORT"] = str(port)
+    os.environ["RANK"] = str(rank)
+    os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"] = str(rank)
+    os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"] = str(_WORLD_SIZE)
+
+    torch.npu.set_device(rank)
+    dist.init_process_group(backend="hccl", rank=rank, world_size=_WORLD_SIZE)
+
+    # The HCCL pg options helper reads the current vLLM config.
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+
+    with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()):
+        _validate_real_hccl_coordinator(_WORLD_SIZE, rank)
+        _validate_coordinator_without_backend(_WORLD_SIZE)
+
+    dist.barrier()
+    dist.destroy_process_group()
+
+
+def test_group_coordinator_destroy_releases_the_hccl_group() -> None:
+    """The destroy path releases the HCCL group exactly once, and still works
+    for a coordinator that was built without ``__init__``."""
+    if torch.npu.device_count() < _WORLD_SIZE:
+        pytest.skip(f"requires {_WORLD_SIZE} NPU devices")
+    mp.spawn(_worker, args=(get_open_port(),), nprocs=_WORLD_SIZE, join=True)

[Feature][A3] Integrate K3.1 DSpark MLA with device-side tiling (#23221)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Integrate the community A3 MLA provider for eligible Kimi K3.1 DSpark
draft decode. The draft prepares a schedule from device lengths with
`get_scheduler_metadata` and passes it to `flash_attn_with_kvcache`. If
the provider or a required entry point is unavailable, the existing
backend handles decode.

A3 FULL proposal skips the metadata result that would be discarded. The
graph manager builds the metadata through the upstream uniform helper
and refreshes the captured schedules once per replay. In split DCP this
refresh prepares one history schedule and one current-token schedule.
Eager and piecewise proposals still build metadata in the normal entry
point.

The connector capability check recognizes a single built-in MooncakeV2
child and applies the existing layerwise restriction. Cache allocation,
writes and backend selection share the final layout decision, including
the validated deployment restrictions for a wrapper.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Supported A3 DSpark draft decode can use the [native
provider](https://github.com/MinghuasLab/flash-attention-npu) without a
new configuration option. The provider-only commit `d20db138e` retains
the corrected token-count copy and next-step event wait for comparison.
The separately reviewable commit `48b57b0df` skips both on eligible A3
Kimi configurations through the existing model-state hooks. At KV
initialization Kimi checks the active consumers. The scheduler keeps its
host upper bound while execution uses corrected device lengths.

This branch supports eligible single-rank decode. Multi-rank split
execution requires the DCP changes in #23220. Without split support it
keeps the existing backend.

### How was this patch tested?

- At `48b57b0df`, 148 CPU attention tests passed and 7 skipped. Combined
with #23220 at `4ff444bad`, the attention and DCP output-mask suites had
157 passes and 17 skips.
- An additional 16 isolated CPU cases passed on both trees. These
exercised the production Kimi hooks and runner copy/update methods with
PyTorch CPU tensors and stand-ins for unavailable runtime dependencies
and stream events. They covered rejection and reordered requests, DCP
sizes 1 and 8, native RecoverSSM on/off, A3 native vs FIA,
reinitialization, unsupported consumers and the existing A5 decision.
- A RecoverSSM page-boundary regression test is included for the full
vLLM environment and was not run locally. This revision has no new NPU
profiling or serving measurement.

+def load_source(path, name):
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, ROOT / path)
+    assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    sys.modules[name] = module
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module

+    nodes = ast.parse((ROOT / path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")).body
+    chosen = []
+    for node in nodes:
+        name = getattr(node, "name", None)
+        if (
+            name in names
+            or isinstance(node, ast.Assign)
+            and any(isinstance(t, ast.Name) and t.id in names for t in node.targets)
+        ):
+            chosen.append(node)
+    assert len(chosen) == len(names), (path, names)
+    exec(compile(ast.Module(body=chosen, type_ignores=[]), str(ROOT / path), "exec"), scope)
+    return scope

+def ast_method(path, owner, name, scope):
+    module = ast.parse((ROOT / path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    cls = next(n for n in module.body if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) and n.name == owner)
+    fn = next(n for n in cls.body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == name)
+    fn.decorator_list = []
+    # Keep implementation intact; remove annotations requiring unavailable vLLM types.
+    fn.returns = None
+    for arg in (*fn.args.posonlyargs, *fn.args.args, *fn.args.kwonlyargs):
+        arg.annotation = None
+    exec(compile(ast.Module(body=[fn], type_ignores=[]), str(ROOT / path), "exec"), scope)
+    return scope[name]

+    # CPU ABI instrumentation only: device rejection is tested above; this does
+    # not simulate or validate the native attention kernel's arithmetic.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(sink.A3MLAAdapter, "_check_lengths", lambda self, lengths, cu, used: lengths.numel())
+    lengths = torch.tensor([1, 0], dtype=torch.int32)

+    used = torch.tensor([2, 0], dtype=torch.int32)
+    calls = []
+    provider_outputs: list[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]] = []
+
+    def metadata_op(*args, **kwargs):
+        assert args[6] is lengths
+        assert kwargs["cu_seqlens_q"] is cu
+        calls.append("metadata")
+        return torch.zeros(32, dtype=torch.uint8)
+
+    def attention_op(q, rope, content, **kwargs):
+        assert kwargs["cache_seqlens"] is lengths
+        assert kwargs["cu_seqlens_q"] is cu
+        assert kwargs["scheduler_metadata"] is metadata
+        assert q.shape == (4, 8, 64) and q.is_contiguous()
+        assert kwargs["qv"].shape == (4, 8, 512) and kwargs["qv"].is_contiguous()
+        calls.append("attention")
+        output = torch.ones(4, 8, 512, dtype=q.dtype)
+        lse = torch.full((8, 4), torch.inf)
+        provider_outputs.append((output, lse))
+        return output, lse, None, None
+
+    adapter = sink.A3MLAAdapter(sink.A3MLAConfig(8, 0.125, mask_mode=3 if causal else 0), attention_op, metadata_op)
+
+    def forbidden(*args, **kwargs):
+        pytest.fail("the adapter must not read host values or remask normalized lengths")
+
+    with monkeypatch.context() as context:
+        for name in ("cpu", "item", "tolist"):
+            context.setattr(torch.Tensor, name, forbidden)
+        context.setattr(torch, "where", forbidden)
+        metadata = adapter.build_metadata(lengths, cu, used)
+        output_mask = adapter.build_output_mask(lengths, cu, 4)
+        context.setattr(torch, "searchsorted", forbidden)
+        context.setattr(torch.Tensor, "masked_fill", forbidden)
+        output, lse = adapter.attention(
+            torch.zeros(4, 8, 576, dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+            adapter.allocate_cache(2, device="cpu"),
+            block_table=torch.zeros(2, 1, dtype=torch.int32),
+            cache_seqlens=lengths,
+            cu_seqlens_q=cu,
+            seqused_q=used,
+            metadata=metadata,
+            output_mask=output_mask,
+        )

+    assert output.data_ptr() == provider_outputs[0][0].data_ptr()
+    assert lse.data_ptr() == provider_outputs[0][1].data_ptr()
+    assert torch.all(output[:, 2:] == 0) and torch.isneginf(lse[:, 2:]).all()
+    assert torch.all(output[:, 1] == 1)
+    assert torch.all(output[:, 0] == (0 if causal else 1))
+    if causal:
+        assert torch.isneginf(lse[:, 0]).all()

+        lengths, cu = args[6], kwargs["cu_seqlens_q"]
+        assert lengths.device.type == "cpu"  # A3 must not use Meta shape inference.
+        calls.append((args[1], args[2], lengths, cu))

+
+    names = {

+        FlashMLAImpl=type("UnusedA5", (), {}),
+        QuantFlashMLAImpl=type("UnusedQuant", (), {}),
+        A3MLAAdapter=sink.A3MLAAdapter,
+        get_dcp_local_seq_lens=lambda lengths, **kwargs: (lengths + 1) // 2,
+    )
+    ast_symbols("vllm_ascend/attention/flashmla.py", names, scope)
+    if dcp_size > 1 and not hasattr(scope["FlashMLACurrent"], "allocate_split"):
+        pytest.skip("requires split-query DCP support")
+    impl = SimpleNamespace(
+        use_quant_flashmla=False,
+        a3_mla_adapter=sink.A3MLAAdapter(sink.A3MLAConfig(8, 0.125), None, metadata_op),

+            speculative_config=object(),
+            parallel_config=SimpleNamespace(cp_kv_cache_interleave_size=1),
+        ),
+    )
+    builder = scope["FlashMLAMetadataBuilder"](impl, torch.device("cpu"), 4, torch.empty(0))
+    inputs = common()
+    inputs.causal = causal
+    first = builder.build(inputs, 2, 3, False, retain_for_graph=True)
+    schedule_ptr = first.schedule.data_ptr()
+    mask_ptr = first.output_mask.data_ptr()
+    current_ptr = first.current.schedule.data_ptr() if first.current else None
+    current_mask_ptr = first.current.output_mask.data_ptr() if first.current else None
+    split = causal and dcp_size > 1
+    assert len(calls) == 1 + int(split)
+    assert first.cache_lens.tolist() == (

+    assert calls[0][2] is first.cache_lens  # Keep the builder's length buffer.

+    second = builder.build(inputs, 2, 3, False)
+    assert len(calls) == 2 * (1 + int(split))

+    assert second.output_mask.data_ptr() == mask_ptr
+    expected_live = [False, False] if split else [not causal, True]

+    assert second.used_q.tolist() == [2, 0, 0, 0, 0]

+    # Reorder query boundaries and reactivate a previously empty request in

+    for _ in range(2):

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""A3 split-Q MLA provider boundary for flash-attention-npu's 910 release.
+
+The existing FlashMLA batch builder owns buffers and stream ordering. This
+adapter translates its normalized inputs without imposing the A5 cache ABI.
+Each packed Q segment is wholly live or wholly padding; the builder sets
+padding KV lengths to zero before either operator consumes them.
+"""
+
+import math
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
+from importlib import import_module
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+
+ROPE_DIM = 64
+LATENT_DIM = 512
+QK_DIM = ROPE_DIM + LATENT_DIM
+PAGE_SIZE = 128
+OPERATOR_MODULE = "flash_attn_npu_3"
+
+
+def get_a3_mla_ops():
+    """Select before cache allocation, following the A5 package availability policy."""
+    try:
+        module = import_module(OPERATOR_MODULE)
+    except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:
+        if exc.name == OPERATOR_MODULE:
+            return None
+        raise
+    attention = getattr(module, "flash_attn_with_kvcache", None)
+    metadata = getattr(module, "get_scheduler_metadata", None)
+    if callable(attention) and callable(metadata):
+        return attention, metadata
+    return None
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class A3MLAConfig:
+    num_heads: int
+    softmax_scale: float
+    mask_mode: int = 3
+    max_seqlen_k: int = PAGE_SIZE
+    max_seqlen_q: int = 1
+    dtype: torch.dtype = torch.bfloat16
+
+    def __post_init__(self):
+        if self.num_heads <= 0 or self.mask_mode not in (0, 3):
+            raise ValueError("A3 MLA requires positive heads, plain/causal mask and ND paged cache")
+        if not math.isfinite(self.softmax_scale):
+            raise ValueError("softmax_scale must be finite")
+        if self.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
+            raise ValueError("A3 MLA supports FP16/BF16")
+        if self.max_seqlen_k <= 0 or self.max_seqlen_k % PAGE_SIZE:
+            raise ValueError("A3 MLA logical KV capacity must be positive and page-aligned")
+        if self.max_seqlen_q < 0:
+            raise ValueError("query capacity must be nonnegative")
+
+
+def supports_a3_mla(impl, *, is_a3: bool, is_draft: bool, supports_pd_layout: Callable[[Any], bool]) -> bool:
+    """Static selection before cache allocation; no tensor-content reads."""
+    if not is_a3 or not is_draft:
+        return False
+    cfg = impl.vllm_config
+    if cfg.model_config.hf_config.model_type != "kimi_k31":
+        return False
+    spec = cfg.speculative_config
+    if not getattr(cfg, "use_v2_model_runner", False) or spec is None or spec.method != "dspark":
+        return False
+    if impl.num_kv_heads != 1 or impl.kv_lora_rank != LATENT_DIM or impl.qk_rope_head_dim != ROPE_DIM:
+        return False
+    if impl.fa_quant_layer or impl.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16) or impl.enable_kv_nz:
+        return False
+    # Split DCP must understand the provider's separate Q/KV components and
+    # normalize empty local rows before merging their LSE contributions.
+    if impl.use_dcp and not getattr(impl, "supports_split_query_dcp", False):
+        return False
+    if impl.use_pcp or cfg.parallel_config.pipeline_parallel_size != 1:
+        return False
+    # The caller shares A5's component-major cache transfer gate. Keep this
+    # provider boundary independent of vLLM's cache/connector imports.
+    if not supports_pd_layout(cfg):
+        return False
+    # AscendMLABackend exposes 128-token kernel pages. Manager blocks (e.g.
+    # K3.1's 1536) are expanded by the existing block-table/cache-view layer;
+    # they are not the operator's page_size argument.
+    return cfg.cache_config.block_size > 0 and cfg.cache_config.block_size % PAGE_SIZE == 0
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class A3MLAAdapter:
+    config: A3MLAConfig
+    attention_op: Any
+    metadata_op: Any
+
+    def allocate_cache(self, pages: int, *, device):
+        """Keep both A3 components packed inside each page, including DCP KV."""
+        shape = (pages, PAGE_SIZE, 1)
+        return (
+            torch.empty((*shape, LATENT_DIM), dtype=self.config.dtype, device=device),
+            torch.empty((*shape, ROPE_DIM), dtype=self.config.dtype, device=device),
+        )
+
+    @classmethod
+    def load(cls, config: A3MLAConfig):
+        ops = get_a3_mla_ops()
+        if ops is None:
+            raise ImportError(
+                "A3 MLA requires a validated build with flash_attn_with_kvcache and get_scheduler_metadata in "
+                + OPERATOR_MODULE
+            )
+        return cls(config, *ops)
+
+    def for_capacity(self, columns: int, tokens: int):
+        return replace(self, config=replace(self.config, max_seqlen_k=columns * PAGE_SIZE, max_seqlen_q=tokens))
+
+    def _check_lengths(self, cache_seqlens, cu_seqlens_q, seqused_q):
+        batch = cache_seqlens.numel()
+        if batch == 0:
+            raise ValueError("A3 MLA requires a nonempty batch")
+        if cache_seqlens.shape != (batch,) or cache_seqlens.dtype != torch.int32:
+            raise ValueError("cache_seqlens must be int32 [B]")
+        if cu_seqlens_q.shape != (batch + 1,) or cu_seqlens_q.dtype != torch.int32:
+            raise ValueError("cu_seqlens_q must be int32 [B+1]")
+        if not cache_seqlens.is_contiguous() or not cu_seqlens_q.is_contiguous():
+            raise ValueError("A3 lengths must be contiguous")
+        if cache_seqlens.device != cu_seqlens_q.device:
+            raise ValueError("A3 lengths must share a device")
+        if seqused_q is not None:
+            if (
+                seqused_q.shape != (batch,)
+                or seqused_q.dtype != torch.int32
+                or seqused_q.device != cache_seqlens.device
+            ):
+                raise ValueError("seqused_q must be same-device int32 [B]")
+            # The builder derives used_q from cu differences, or sets a whole
+            # dummy segment to zero. Partial segments are not representable by
+            # this public operator ABI. Do not read device values here:
+            # aten::_assert_async falls back to CPU on torch_npu 2.10.
+        if cache_seqlens.device.type != "npu":
+            raise ValueError("native A3 MLA requires NPU tensors")
+        return batch
+
+    def build_metadata(self, cache_seqlens, cu_seqlens_q, seqused_q=None):
+        # FlashMLAMetadataBuilder zeros dummy-request lengths once per batch.
+        # Both operators consume that same tensor; do not remask it per layer.
+        batch = self._check_lengths(cache_seqlens, cu_seqlens_q, seqused_q)
+        cfg = self.config
+        metadata = self.metadata_op(
+            batch,
+            cfg.max_seqlen_q,
+            cfg.max_seqlen_k,
+            cfg.num_heads,
+            1,
+            ROPE_DIM,
+            cache_seqlens,
+            qkv_dtype=cfg.dtype,
+            headdim_v=LATENT_DIM,
+            cu_seqlens_q=cu_seqlens_q,
+            page_size=PAGE_SIZE,
+            causal=cfg.mask_mode == 3,
+            num_splits=1,
+        )
+        if (
+            not isinstance(metadata, torch.Tensor)
+            or metadata.dtype != torch.uint8
+            or metadata.ndim != 1
+            or not metadata.is_contiguous()
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("A3 provider metadata must be a contiguous opaque uint8 vector")
+        if not metadata.numel() or metadata.device != cache_seqlens.device:
+            raise ValueError("A3 provider metadata must be nonempty and remain on the input device")
+        return metadata
+
+    def build_output_mask(self, cache_seqlens, cu_seqlens_q, num_tokens):
+        """Rows without visible KV, shared across layers for one refreshed batch."""
+        token = torch.arange(num_tokens, device=cache_seqlens.device, dtype=torch.int32)
+        request = torch.searchsorted(cu_seqlens_q[1:].contiguous(), token, right=True).long()
+        lengths = cache_seqlens[request]
+        invalid = lengths <= 0
+        if self.config.mask_mode == 3:
+            query_start = cu_seqlens_q[request]
+            query_lengths = cu_seqlens_q[request + 1] - query_start
+            invalid |= lengths - query_lengths + token - query_start < 0
+        return invalid
+
+    def attention(
+        self,
+        q,
+        k_cache,
+        *,
+        block_table,
+        cache_seqlens,
+        cu_seqlens_q,
+        metadata,
+        output_mask,
+        seqused_q=None,
+        attn_mask=None,
+        normalize_output=True,
+        return_softmax_lse=True,
+    ):

[Feature][Sleep Mode] Discard parameter-only weights at level 2 (#22629)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This is the P2 follow-up to the merged P1 integration (#22822) of
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/22572. P1 moved
Ascend sleep/wake onto `SleepModeBackend`; this PR implements the
upstream
discardable level-2 contract so level 2 no longer keeps Python copies of
the
whole model.

Changes:

- Discard only weights allocations whose blocks are exclusively
rewritten
parameters or inactive. Mixed and non-parameter allocations are backed
up
  to host and restored on wake-up.
- Keep `sleep_preserve_parameter_names` semantics by excluding preserved
  parameter storages from the discardable set.
- Remove the Python level-2 parameter/buffer snapshots; the allocator's
CPU
  backups now provide the restore path.
- Align `CaMemAllocator.sleep`, `discard`, `wake_up`, and
`use_memory_pool`
  with the upstream structure, using NPU CPU backup, memcpy, and unmap
  primitives, including the CPU backup release hook.
- Remove Ascend's local `_get_sleep_parameters()` / `get_draft_model()`
  overrides and inherit the upstream implementations. 

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, the sleep-mode memory policy changes, but the public API/CLI is
unchanged.

- **Level 2:**
- Parameter-only weights allocations are discarded without a CPU backup
and
    restored by the caller's weight reload.
- Mixed and non-parameter weights-pool allocations are backed up to CPU
and
restored on wake-up instead of being discarded with the whole weights
pool.
- `sleep_preserve_parameter_names` continues to retain selected
parameters.
- Draft parameters are now included as `draft.*`, matching upstream.
Callers
should preserve them with `sleep_preserve_parameter_names=["draft.*"]`
or
    restore them through the separate draft weight-update path.

- **Level 1:**
- Weights and `runtime` / `cudagraph` allocations are backed up, while
KV
    cache and other non-offloaded tags are discarded.
- This matches upstream `CuMemBackend.suspend()`. Ascend currently tags
only
`weights` and `kv_cache`, so there is no observable level-1 change in
    current models; the additional tags are for future runtime/cudagraph
    allocations.

- `--enable-sleep-mode` and the sleep/wake API are unchanged.

A release note is added in `release_notes/fragments/22629.yaml`.

### Compatibility and limitations

- **torch_npu 2.10:** `MemPool.snapshot()` is unavailable, so the
allocator
uses `torch.npu.memory_snapshot()` and filters to live weights
allocations.
  Per-pool snapshots can replace this fallback once torch_npu 2.13 is
  supported.
- Because per-pool snapshots are unavailable on the current pin,
  `CaMemAllocator._trim` and `CaMemAllocator.cudagraph_pool` raise
  `NotImplementedError`; `use_memory_pool` does not call `_trim`.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Environment:

```
Ascend 910
vLLM v0.34.0 (62d4bc3c7e) + export VLLM_VERSION=0.34.0
torch_npu 2.10.0.post7
Current sleep-backend-p1 branch
```

#### Relevant CPU UT

```bash
pytest -q \
  tests/ut/worker \
  tests/ut/device_allocator \
  tests/ut/test_platform.py

# 2666 passed, 10 skipped
```

#### Sleep E2E

```bash
pytest -sv \
  tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/rlhf/state_transitions/test_sleep_wake.py

# 3 passed in 159.01s
```

Observed:

```text
Using sleep-mode backend: camem
Sleep mode (level=1) freed 46.58 GiB
Sleep mode (level=2) freed 46.58 GiB
```

#### Level-2 discard / reload E2E

```bash
pytest -sv \
  tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/rlhf/state_transitions/test_sleep_level2_reload.py

# 2 passed in 58.21s
```

Coverage:

- level-2 discard + target reload restores the greedy output;
- a preserved embedding parameter is restored by
`wake_up(tags=["weights"])`
  without a reload.

Observed:

```text
Sleep mode (level=2) freed 19.14 GiB
Sleep mode (level=2) freed 19.23 GiB
```

#### Draft preserve E2E

Configuration:

```text
Target: Qwen3-1.7B
Draft:  Qwen3-1.7B_eagle3
sleep_preserve_parameter_names: ["draft.*"]
```

Flow:

```text
generate
sleep(level=2)
wake_up(tags=["weights"])
reload_weights
wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"])
generate
```

Result:

```text
before: Paris. The capital
after:  Paris. The capital

DRAFT_SLEEP_E2E_OK
```

This confirms that `draft.*` parameters are excluded from the
discardable set,
backed up, and restored while target parameters are discarded and
reloaded.
