[Feature][HiSparse] Mooncake MemFabric Pull into shared Offload Host (#22109)

## What changes

Extend #20926 with direct P/D Pull from ordinary Prefill KV into
HiSparse on Decode. Set `transfer_backend=memfabric` in
`MooncakeConnectorV2` to select the native MemFabric TransferEngine.
Decode pulls MLA main KV directly into its MemFabric Offload Host Source
and Indexer KV into each rank's NPU.

- In shared mode, Decode TP rank 0 contributes the shared Host backing,
imports main KV and writes new main KV back. Other ranks attach to the
backing. Each rank keeps its own Indexer, Resident and Hot buffers.
- The transfer engine registers Prefill source regions and Decode
destinations. On Decode, it registers the entire Host allocation once,
including padding.
- URMA requests reuse a selected Prefill KV replica to reduce concurrent
session setup. P and D use matching TP. Decode requires PCP=1 and
Prefill requires DCP=1. Prefill PCP>1 is covered by targeted address
tests and still needs end-to-end NPU validation.

## Core pairing and Ascend Worker

Build with unmodified [vLLM Core
`c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15),
pinned in `.github/vllm-main-verified.commit`.

- `AscendHiSparseConnectorWorker` extends the upstream HiSparse worker
with Ascend DMA setup, recycled-block invalidation, H→D DMA for batched
Host-to-Resident restore, and TP synchronization for rank-0 Host
writeback.
- `AscendHiSparseOffloadManager` takes the engine configuration from the
existing `HiSparseHostPool` instance and owns the physical Host
allocation and sharing.
- The Decode `MultiConnector` combination can overlap Target Host
writeback with MTP drafting and waits for the Host copy before reporting
readiness.

## A5 startup example

On each node, set `MODEL_PATH` to the local GLM-5.2 W4A8C8 model
directory and `VLLM_HOST_IP` to the node's own reachable address. The
example uses TP8 and PCP=1 on both sides. Send inference requests
through a P/D proxy.

```bash
# Run on both nodes in the matching vLLM Ascend environment.
export MODEL_PATH=/path/to/GLM-5.2-W4A8C8
export VLLM_HOST_IP='REPLACE_WITH_LOCAL_NODE_IP'
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
COMMON_ARGS=(
  --served-model-name glm52-w4a8c8 --host "$VLLM_HOST_IP"
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --dtype bfloat16 --quantization ascend
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 128 --max-model-len 139264
  --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 --max-num-seqs 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8
  --reasoning-parser glm47
)
```

**Prefill (ordinary KV, eager)**

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" "${COMMON_ARGS[@]}" --port 18100 \
  --enforce-eager --enable-prefix-caching \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV2", "kv_role":"kv_producer", "kv_port":31300,
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{"transfer_backend":"memfabric","memfabric_transfer_protocol":"device_urma"}
  }'
```

**Decode (HiSparse, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`)**

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" "${COMMON_ARGS[@]}" --port 18101 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8]}' \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8","hisparse_config":{"eager_host_mirror":true}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector":"MultiConnector", "kv_role":"kv_consumer", "kv_port":31400,
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[
      {"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer",
        "kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":32.0}},
      {"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV2","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_port":31400,
        "kv_connector_extra_config":{"transfer_backend":"memfabric","memfabric_transfer_protocol":"device_urma"}}
    ]}
  }'
```

Keep `HiSparseConnector` first in the Decode `MultiConnector` list. To
reproduce the MTP functional check, add `--speculative-config
'{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'` to both commands.

## Full-model A5 validation

Validated at `820de494de` with GLM-5.2 W4A8C8 and TP8 per node. Prefill
ran in eager mode with HiSparse disabled. Decode used HiSparse with
`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`. Transfer used native MemFabric `1.5.0.dev20261115`
with `transfer_backend=memfabric` and
`memfabric_transfer_protocol=device_urma`.

- **GPQA Diamond** — 178/198 correct (89.90%). All 198 requests
returned. Six responses hit the 131,072-token limit. No MemFabric
connection failures were observed during the concurrency-8 resume.
- **Prefill-only** — 65,536 input tokens, one output token, zero
prefix-cache hits. All 24 requests passed at concurrency 1. Mean/P90
TTFT was 16.758/16.773 s. Input throughput was 3,908.42 tokens/s.
- **Decode-only** — 65,536 prefix tokens cached per request, one
additional token computed for initial logits, and 1,024 output tokens.
All 24 requests passed at concurrency 1. Mean/P90 TTFT was 143.83/151.32
ms, mean TPOT was 24.40 ms, and output throughput was 40.79 tokens/s.
- **P/D + HiSparse + MTP** — All eight requests with 301- or 2,100-token
inputs matched the non-MTP continuations. Decode confirmed KV Pull,
target and draft graph replay, and overlap of rank-0 Host writeback with
drafting. MTP accepted 24 of 45 proposed tokens. High-concurrency MTP
performance remains untested.

## Earlier reduced-model measurements

An earlier A5 eager run with 10-layer GLM-5.3 MXFP8 and P/D TP2 matched
local Decode on eight-token continuations for 5, 301, 2,049, 4,097 and
8,193 input tokens, plus a repeated 301-token request. It recorded
62,050 Host refill misses and 101,299,520 Host-to-device bytes. Both
Decode ranks mapped the same 1 GiB Host backing. A separate earlier
pairing also matched these cases with `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` and capture
size 1.

## Scope and qualification

This PR covers bulk Pull. AscendStore pooling and layerwise transfer are
outside its scope. Shared Host allocation requires a single Decode node
with multiprocessing and PP=PCP=DCP=1. The results above are tied to
their tested revisions and configurations. The current Core pairing
still needs end-to-end NPU qualification.

AI assistance was used for implementation, investigation, tests and this
description.

+"""Pull P KV into HiSparse's Host Source and NPU Indexer groups."""
+
+import ctypes

+from collections.abc import Callable
+from dataclasses import replace
+from functools import partial
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import KVCacheConfig
+
+from vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_p2p.mooncake.connector import MooncakePullConnector
+from vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_p2p.mooncake.metadata import MooncakeTransferMetadata
+from vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_p2p.mooncake.pull_worker import (
+    MooncakePullRecvingThread,
+    _MemFabricPullWorker,
+)
+from vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_p2p.mooncake.utils import (
+    as_kv_cache_tensors,
+)

+
+
+class _HiSparsePullThread(MooncakePullRecvingThread):
+    def _append_spec_transfer_addresses(
+        self,
+        spec_index,
+        remote_pcp_rank,
+        remote_tp_rank,
+        remote_pcp_size,
+        remote_tp_size,
+        remote_dcp_size,
+        transfer_entries_by_layer,
+        remote_metadata,
+        src_list,
+        dst_list,
+        length_list,
+    ) -> Callable[[], None] | None:
+        if remote_tp_size != self.tp_size or self.pcp_size != 1 or remote_dcp_size != 1:
+            raise ValueError("HiSparse Pull requires equal P/D TP, D PCP=1, and P DCP=1")
+        host_layers = {
+            pair: entries
+            for pair, entries in transfer_entries_by_layer.items()
+            if self.kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[self.group_indices[pair[0]]].host_resident
+        }
+        ordinary = {pair: entries for pair, entries in transfer_entries_by_layer.items() if pair not in host_layers}
+        if ordinary:
+            super()._append_spec_transfer_addresses(
+                spec_index,
+                remote_pcp_rank,
+                remote_tp_rank,
+                remote_pcp_size,
+                remote_tp_size,
+                remote_dcp_size,
+                ordinary,
+                remote_metadata,
+                src_list,
+                dst_list,
+                length_list,
+            )
+        if not host_layers:
+            return None
+
+        pages_to_reorder: dict[int, tuple[int, int, int]] = {}
+        spec = self.kv_cache_specs[spec_index]
+        peer = remote_metadata.metadata_by_pcp_rank[remote_pcp_rank].metadata_by_tp_rank[remote_tp_rank]
+        for (local_index, remote_index), entries in host_layers.items():
+            self._append_host_layer_reads(
+                spec,
+                local_index,
+                remote_index,
+                peer.kv_caches_base_addr[remote_index],
+                remote_metadata,
+                entries,
+                local_dsts=src_list,
+                remote_srcs=dst_list,
+                lengths=length_list,
+                pages_to_reorder=pages_to_reorder,
+            )
+        return partial(self._reorder_host_pages, pages_to_reorder) if pages_to_reorder else None
+
+    def _append_host_layer_reads(
+        self,
+        spec,
+        local_index,
+        remote_index,
+        remote_bases,
+        remote_metadata,
+        entries,
+        *,
+        local_dsts,
+        remote_srcs,
+        lengths,
+        pages_to_reorder,
+    ):
+        row_bytes, components = self._host_pull_components(
+            spec, local_index, remote_index, remote_bases, remote_metadata
+        )
+        local_base = self.kv_caches_base_addr[local_index][0]
+        local_stride = self.block_strides[local_index][0]
+        for _, local_blocks, remote_blocks in entries:
+            for local_block, remote_block in zip(local_blocks, remote_blocks, strict=True):
+                local_page = local_base + local_block * local_stride
+                if self._append_host_page_reads(
+                    local_page, remote_block, components, spec.block_size, row_bytes, local_dsts, remote_srcs, lengths
+                ):
+                    pages_to_reorder[local_page] = (spec.block_size, row_bytes, components[0][2])
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _append_host_page_reads(
+        local_page, remote_block, components, tokens_per_page, row_bytes, local_dsts, remote_srcs, lengths
+    ):
+        remote_pages = [
+            (base + remote_block * stride, token_bytes, row_offset)
+            for base, stride, token_bytes, row_offset in components
+        ]
+        # MemFabric READ accepts local destinations before remote sources.
+        if len(remote_pages) == 1:
+            remote_page, _, _ = remote_pages[0]
+            local_dsts.append(local_page)
+            remote_srcs.append(remote_page)
+            lengths.append(tokens_per_page * row_bytes)
+            return
+        offset = 0
+        for remote_page, token_bytes, _ in remote_pages:
+            component_bytes = tokens_per_page * token_bytes
+            local_dsts.append(local_page + offset)
+            remote_srcs.append(remote_page)
+            lengths.append(component_bytes)
+            offset += component_bytes
+        return True
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _reorder_host_pages(pages: dict[int, tuple[int, int, int]]) -> None:
+        scratch = np.empty(max(tokens * row_bytes for tokens, row_bytes, _ in pages.values()), dtype=np.uint8)
+        for local_page, (tokens, row_bytes, first_component_bytes) in pages.items():
+            page_bytes = tokens * row_bytes
+            page = np.frombuffer((ctypes.c_uint8 * page_bytes).from_address(local_page), dtype=np.uint8)
+            source = scratch[:page_bytes]
+            source[:] = page
+            rows = page.reshape(tokens, row_bytes)
+            rows[:, :first_component_bytes] = source[: tokens * first_component_bytes].reshape(
+                tokens, first_component_bytes
+            )
+            rows[:, first_component_bytes:] = source[tokens * first_component_bytes :].reshape(
+                tokens, row_bytes - first_component_bytes
+            )
+
+    def _host_pull_components(self, spec, local_index, remote_index, bases, remote_metadata):
+        """Describe P's MLA components and their offsets within a D Host row."""
+        if len(self.kv_caches_base_addr[local_index]) != 1 or len(bases) not in (1, 2):
+            raise ValueError("HiSparse Pull requires one Host Source and one or two P components")
+
+        tokens = spec.block_size
+        sizes = remote_metadata.block_lens[remote_index]
+        strides = remote_metadata.block_strides[remote_index]
+        if len(bases) == 1 and len(remote_metadata.block_shapes[remote_index][0]) == 1:
+            # Component-major MLA is advertised as one flat slot.
+            hf = self.model_config.hf_text_config
+            latent_bytes = tokens * hf.kv_lora_rank * spec.dtype.itemsize
+            rope_bytes = tokens * hf.qk_rope_head_dim * spec.dtype.itemsize
+            if latent_bytes + rope_bytes > sizes[0]:
+                raise ValueError("P MLA slot is smaller than its NoPE/RoPE payload")
+            bases = [bases[0], bases[0] + latent_bytes]
+            sizes = [latent_bytes, rope_bytes]
+            strides = [strides[0], strides[0]]
+
+        page_bytes = self.block_lens[local_index][0]
+        if sum(sizes) != page_bytes or any(size % tokens for size in sizes):
+            raise ValueError("HiSparse Pull MLA component sizes differ from Host Source")
+
+        row_offset = 0
+        components = []
+        for base, stride, size in zip(bases, strides, sizes, strict=True):
+            token_bytes = size // tokens
+            components.append((base, stride, token_bytes, row_offset))
+            row_offset += token_bytes
+        return row_offset, components

+        if self.kv_transfer_config.is_kv_consumer:
+            self._prepare_destination_caches(caches, transfer_group_ids)

+        # Keep group IDs and allocation geometry intact while narrowing the
+        # layer list seen by the ordinary Mooncake registration flow.
+        tensors = []
+        for tensor in config.kv_cache_tensors:
+            layers = [name for name in get_kv_cache_tensor_layers(tensor) if name not in excluded_layers]
+            if not layers:

+            for name in layers:

+                    if cache.shape[0] % logical_blocks:

+    def _prepare_destination_caches(

+    ) -> None:
+        config = self.kv_cache_config
+        context = self.vllm_config.compilation_config.static_forward_context
+        host_group_ids = transfer_group_ids.intersection(config.host_group_ids)
+        source_parts = [
+            cache
+            for group_id in host_group_ids
+            for name in config.kv_cache_groups[group_id].layer_names
+            for cache in as_kv_cache_tensors(caches[name])
+        ]
+        if host_group_ids and (not source_parts or any(cache.device.type != "cpu" for cache in source_parts)):
+            raise ValueError("HiSparse PD Source must consist of Host tensors")
+        self._host_pool_regions = {
+            cache.untyped_storage().data_ptr(): cache.untyped_storage().nbytes() for cache in source_parts
+        }
+        for group_id in transfer_group_ids:
+            group = config.kv_cache_groups[group_id]
+            if group.role == "hisparse_indexer":
+                for name in group.layer_names:
+                    stride = getattr(context[name], "hisparse_block_stride", 1)
+                    if stride > 1:

+
+    def _create_recving_thread(self, ready_event: threading.Event) -> MooncakePullRecvingThread:
+        metadata = self.xfer_handshake_metadata
+        assert isinstance(metadata, MooncakeTransferMetadata)
+        config = self.kv_cache_config
+        host_groups = set(config.host_group_ids)
+        host_blocks = config.hisparse_host_num_blocks

[Doc] ucm document update (#23436)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Every `vllm serve` example in the UCM Store Deployment Guide hardcodes
`--max-model-len 17000`. That ceiling is below the workloads the same
page
documents, so the deployment steps and the results that follow them are
mutually inconsistent:

- **The performance table reports 32K, 64K and 128K input scenarios.**
All
three exceed 17,000 tokens, so a reader who starts the service with the
documented command cannot reproduce a single row — the requests are
rejected
by the context limit before UCM is ever exercised. The 128K row alone
needs
128K input + 1K output ≈ 132K tokens, roughly seven times the advertised
  limit.
- **The remaining examples are about long-context external reuse**,
which a
  17K ceiling largely precludes.

This PR sets each example to a value appropriate to the model it
deploys:

| Model | Sections | `--max-model-len` | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| QwQ-32B | Centralized PD (Prefill, Decode); Distributed PD / P2P
(Prefill, Decode); PD-Mixed Inference | `40960` | Comfortably covers the
8K prompts these sections benchmark, instead of advertising a 17K
ceiling |
| GLM-5.1-w4a8 | Large Scale Expert Parallelism (Prefill, Decode) |
`202752` | Must cover the 32K / 64K / 128K rows reported in this guide;
128K + 1K needs at least ~132K |

### Modifications

- `docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/ucm_deployment.md`: replace
  `--max-model-len 17000` in all seven example command blocks —
  `40960` in 5 blocks (QwQ-32B), `202752` in 2 blocks (GLM-5.1-w4a8).
- Verified no `17000` remains and the file contains exactly seven
  `--max-model-len` lines, all updated.
- No other content is touched.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Documentation only — no code, defaults, release notes, or runtime
behavior
change. Users who copy the commands now get a 40K (QwQ-32B) or 198K
(GLM-5.1-w4a8) context limit instead of 17K.

### How was this patch tested?

Documentation-only change; no runtime test applies.

- Confirmed all seven command blocks are updated and no `17000`
occurrence
  remains in the file.
- Confirmed the GLM-5.1 value covers the largest scenario this guide
reports:
  128K input + 1K output ≈ 132K tokens < 202752.
- Confirmed `202752` is the 198K value already used for GLM-5.1 in the
repo:

`tests/e2e/cases/models/configs/GLM/GLM-5.1-W8A8C8-A3_198k_function.yaml`
  runs `--max-model-len 202752`.
- Confirmed the QwQ-32B sections' benchmark commands use
  `--random-input-len 8000`, which the new limit amply covers.

[Doc] Document layer-level MMRS eligibility matrix for MiniMax-M3 and Kimi-K3 (#23424)

﻿### What this PR does / why we need it?

The sequence parallelism guide's "Matmul reduce-scatter fusion" section
only described the graph-level `fuse_gemm_comms` pass. MiniMax-M3
(`SequenceParallelMMReduceScatterOp` in `vllm_ascend/ops/mmrs.py`) and
Kimi-K3 (`KimiOProjMMReduceScatterOp` in `vllm_ascend/ops/linear_op.py`)
additionally install a fused custom op on the attention O-projection
automatically when sequence parallelism is active, with per-model
eligibility gates.

This PR restructures the section into "Graph fusion" (existing text,
unchanged) and "Layer-level O-projection fusion", and documents the
current eligibility matrix (hardware platform/capability, TP sizes,
K/token ranges, weight format, batch type, PCP/DCP, TP sharding and RS
contracts, forward context, underlying torch_npu interface) for both
models, mirroring the gates in the two ops.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Documentation-only update; no release note fragment needed.

### How was this patch tested?

Documentation-only change; no code or behavior changed. The matrix was
cross-checked against the gates in `vllm_ascend/ops/mmrs.py`,
`vllm_ascend/ops/linear_op.py`,
`vllm_ascend/models/minimax_m3/minimax_m3.py`,
`vllm_ascend/models/kimi_k3/kimi_k3.py`, and
`vllm_ascend/device/hardware_profile.py` on main. CI testing only
(markdownlint runs in CI).

[Revert][CI] Revert "Bump CANN base image to 9.3.0_20261125184600" (#23483)

## Summary

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | Revert / CI / Infra |
| Reverted PR | #23362 `[Feature] Bump CANN base image to
9.3.0_20261125184600` |
| Revert commit | `e1c87bfda` |
| Command | `git revert e1c87bfda` |
| Goal | Restore the Nightly baseline and isolate CANN 9.3.0 for further
validation |
| Platforms | A2 / A3 / A5 / 310P (Ubuntu and OpenEuler) |

This revert is a mitigation step to restore a known-good baseline. It
does not change the requirement to adopt CANN 9.3.0; the upgrade will be
re-landed through staged validation.

## Background

#23362 upgraded the base image from CANN 9.3.0 to `9.3.0_20261125184600`
and updated the related Dockerfiles, runner image tags, and csrc cache
targets. It affects all platforms and all Nightly jobs.

## Problem Summary

After #23362, Nightly on commit `97af565` showed broad failures across
platforms:

- A2: Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16/W8A8 performance below `0.97 * baseline`.
- A3: multiple PD multi-node cases failed (`test_multi_node`,
AssertionError / RuntimeError).
- A5: server startup `RuntimeError` and one job exceeded the `2h` limit.
- A3 logs were masked by `obsutil Upload failed (Succeed 0 / Failed 2)`.

The failure window matches the merge of #23362, and the impact spans all
platforms, so a revert is the fastest way to restore a comparable
baseline.

Note: the OpenEuler image build failure caused by yum is not the cause
of these failures. Nightly tests use the Ubuntu images.

## Revert Scope

Revert the full `e1c87bfda`, including:

- `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.a3`, `Dockerfile.a5`, `Dockerfile.310p`, and
their OpenEuler variants
- `.github/workflows/scripts/runner_label.json`
- `.github/workflows/scripts/csrc_cache_targets.json`
- `.github/workflows/_ensure_csrc_cache.yaml`
- `.github/workflows/pr_test.yaml`
- `.github/workflows/schedule_main2main.yaml`

After the revert, runner image tags and csrc cache targets return to the
CANN 9.1.0 baseline.

Out of scope:

[Refactor] Remove remaining Model Runner V1 EPLB implementation (#22244)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Main removed Model Runner V1, but its EPLB implementation and
shared-component branches remain. This PR removes that dependency chain
while retaining the supported V2 execution path:

- Delete `vllm_ascend/eplb`, its policies, adaptor, updater, transfer
worker, and dedicated tests/examples.
- Remove the non-daemon executor patch, dedicated process group/HCCL
setting, metric hooks, NetLoader layer-registry cleanup and legacy V1
bypass fallback, expert-offload V1 `dynamic_eplb` check, collection
state, static-map loading, and legacy quant-method branches.
- Remove V1/V2 EPLB gates and the retired runner marker from shared MoE
execution, router construction, warmup registration, quant methods,
validation, and initial-layout patch consumers. Initial replica
placement and checkpoint loading still obtain the actual EP size.
- Remove the unused `MoeRouterInput.log2phy` field and the redundant
cross-layer `dynamic_eplb` flag from `MoEFusedExpertsInput`,
`build_fused_experts_input`, and `MoEMlpComputeInput` (quantization
methods read their own `self.use_expert_weight_list` directly for
persistent EPLB/MegaMoe weight lists, W8A8/W8A8FP8 kernel selection, and
quantized MoE LoRA validation). V2 keeps its upstream expert map,
router-state mapping, load recording, expert-weight views, and placement
updates.
- Drop ignored V1 controls from launch configurations while preserving
their effective V2 EPLB settings. This cleanup does not enable EPLB, add
redundant slots, or choose a new load window/step interval for those
launchers. Existing explicit V2 EPLB E2E scenarios remain enabled.
- Clean test names/tags, regenerate the coverage report, and update
current documentation, translations, architecture context, and
CODEOWNERS entries (including adding `@freyfwt` as co-owner for
`/vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe` and the MoE patch modules). Historical
release notes are unchanged.

The V2 runner/controller, distributed EPLB state/policies/communicators,
routing operators, and Triton kernels are unchanged. The PCP draft
helper changes only its docstring. MXFP8 selects persistent EPLB lists
in its quant-method weight accessors via `self.use_expert_weight_list`,
and the extended test verifies those lists reach the actual GMM hook.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Remove the retired V1 EPLB package, controls (`DYNAMIC_EPLB`,
`EXPERT_MAP_RECORD`, and legacy `additional_config.eplb_config` fields),
and `eplb:*` MS Service Metrics. Configure EPLB with `--enable-eplb` and
`--eplb-config`; Ascend additional configuration retains
`load_collection_phase` and `stair_config`. Release-note fragment:
`release_notes/fragments/22244.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

- Rebase & post-rebase verification on `2acaf40bd` (onto `main`
`9b8c54e0d` with verified vLLM commit
`c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15`):
- CPU unit tests: **1,298 passed** in the latest
MoE/LoRA/quantization/310P/EPLB/CODEOWNERS verification (on top of the
**1,878 passed** post-rebase sweep across `tests/ut/distributed/eplb`,
`tests/ut/distributed/expert_transfer`,
`tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/test_eplb_map_warmup.py`,
`tests/ut/model_loader/netloader`,
`tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_state.py`,
`tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v4_dspark_eplb.py`,
`tests/ut/models/test_kimi_k3_eplb.py`, `tests/ut/ops/*moe*`,
`tests/ut/ops/test_allgather_eplb.py`,
`tests/ut/ops/test_routed_experts.py`,
`tests/ut/ops/test_token_dispatcher.py`,
`tests/ut/patch/platform/test_initial_expert_layout.py`,
`tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_fused_moe.py`,
`tests/ut/quantization/methods`, `tests/ut/_310p`,
`tests/ut/worker/v2/test_eplb_*`, `tests/ut/lora`,
`tests/ut/observability/test_ms_metrics_provider.py`,
`tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py`, `tests/ut/test_platform.py`, and
`.github/workflows/scripts/test_codeowner_gate.py`).
- Pre-commit (`--hook-stage manual`, including `ruff`, `codespell`,
`typos`, `markdownlint`, `gitleaks`), `mypy` on rebased/updated modules,
`codeowner_gate.py check-coverage`, `.po` message-catalog validation,
and regenerated 494-entry `tests/e2e/coverage.html` all passed; retired
V1 EPLB symbols are absent across tracked source, tests, and current
documentation.

Earlier pre-rebase CPU and real-NPU checks (against `main` `4be68c18c`
and recorded vLLM commit `ba15685ab7f4f5fbed8630bbb7441f8837e76fbe`):

- `bash format.sh ci`: passed, including Markdown and secret scanning.
- CI follow-up in `d2a1d7fb6`: remove the obsolete `get_ascend_config`
mock from `test_swiglu_mx_quant.py`. The removed V1 import made all 67
activation tests fail during fixture setup. This commit changes one test
line and no production code.
- Follow-up CPU pytest: **400 passed** across
`tests/ut/quantization/methods/w8a8`, `tests/ut/ops/test_moe_mlp.py`,
`tests/ut/ops/test_moe_runtime_args.py`, `tests/ut/distributed/eplb`,
`tests/ut/worker/v2/test_eplb_controller.py`, and
`tests/ut/worker/v2/test_eplb_load_collection_phase.py`. Targeted mypy
of `test_swiglu_mx_quant.py` passed.
- GitHub CI on `cf2936ab0`: pre-commit, full mypy for Python
3.10/3.11/3.12, documentation builds, and documentation link checks
passed. CPU UT reported 69 failures against vLLM v0.33.0 and 70 against
the verified main commit. Both include the 67 stale-mock failures fixed
above and two `test_gdn_window_guard.py` failures caused by conflicting
existing FLA version declarations. Those two failures reproduce on the
unchanged main base. The verified-main job also reported one Mooncake
bilateral-transfer test failure; that case passed in an isolated
main-base run. The owning sources, tests, and dependency declarations
for these remaining failures are unchanged by this PR.
- Focused contracts/MXFP8/310P run: **84 passed, 11 skipped**:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/ut/quantization/methods/w8a8/test_w8a8_mxfp8.py \
  tests/ut/ops/test_moe_runtime_args.py \
  tests/ut/ops/test_token_dispatcher.py \
  tests/ut/ops/test_moe_comm_method.py \
  tests/ut/_310p/quantization/test_w8a8_dynamic_moe_310.py \
  tests/ut/_310p/fused_moe/test_shared_fused_moe_310.py
```

- Static review: 22 selected methods have equivalent ASTs after
selecting the supported V2 branch and normalizing the renamed internal
flag. Effective V2 arguments in all four changed SIT YAML files match
the main base after removing controls that V2 ignored. Historical
release notes and the V2 core paths above have no diff.
- Supplementary real-NPU E2E comparison: main base `4be68c18c` and PR
head `d2a1d7fb6`, with the same pinned vLLM commit above, both passed
the full Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16 model on four A5 NPUs (DP2 x TP2 / EP4). The
retained V2 path used asynchronous scheduling, asynchronous EPLB, STAIR,
HIXL, and FULL/PIECEWISE graph capture with active ACL graph replay.
Both completed a real EPLB cycle across all 48 MoE layers (1,457 rank
transfers); each answered all 8 checks correctly before migration and
all 8 after the committed cycle. Baseline and PR token IDs and text
matched exactly for all 16 responses.
- The paired BF16 check reused the existing
`test_qwen3_moe_w8a8_dp2_tp2_async_eplb_accuracy` scenario with
test-only adaptations: BF16 weights without quantization, a bounded
512-chunk wait that stops on the committed-cycle marker, acceptance of
the equivalent answer prefix `called January`, and 8 extra post-cycle
queries. No production source was patched. Source snapshots were checked
against every tracked Git blob. Both lanes reused the same native
extension/custom operators because their native/build sources are
identical.
- Genuine MXFP8 real-NPU E2E: the same base/head and pinned vLLM both
passed a full 35B hybrid MoE model with `W8A8_MXFP8` weights on four A5
NPUs (DP2 x TP2 / EP4), using asynchronous scheduling, asynchronous
EPLB, STAIR and HIXL. Each completed a real committed cycle across all
40 MoE layers with 1,411 rank transfers and passed all 8 factual
answer-prefix checks before migration plus all 8 after migration. An
additional unchanged-base repeat also passed the same checks and
migration.
- MXFP8 provenance: every checkpoint shard/tensor header was checked;
all four workers in each run selected
`AscendW8A8MXFP8DynamicFusedMoEMethod`, with FP8 E4M3 expert weights and
E8M0 scales. All three runs had identical quant-method/tensor metadata.
Runtime: official `nightly-main-a5` image, index digest
`sha256:846dc2c656e86381c007472696c6441a74e8681b8c3e361ead3d209144bc2caa`,
CANN 9.3.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post7. Tracked base/head/vLLM source blobs
matched before and after execution; production code was not patched.
- This MXFP8 run adapted the same repository E2E scenario with test-only
weight selection, text-only inputs, eager execution, the bounded
committed-cycle wait, the equivalent January prefix, and post-cycle
queries. A read-only worker extension checked quantization metadata. The
original real free-memory gate was retained; its probe process exited
directly after success to avoid an interpreter-finalization failure.
Eager was used because this hybrid model's existing causal-convolution
fallback warns that decode-FULL capture stalls; MXFP8 graph execution is
not covered.
- MXFP8 output comparison: all 8 pre-migration responses matched exactly
in token IDs and text between base/head. After migration, 4/8 full
responses matched exactly; unchanged-base vs unchanged-base repeat
matched 5/8 after migration. All answer-prefix checks passed in every
run, so this scenario is not token-reproducible even on the unchanged
base. No PR-specific initialization, quantization-selection,
committed-migration or answer-prefix failure was observed. This does not
establish bitwise equivalence or full model accuracy; other MXFP
formats, MXFP8 graph execution, other hardware, cross-node execution and
performance remain outside this comparison.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Existing layout, redundancy,
phase-filtering, and configuration tests ran.
- [x] **Regression test**: Real routed-expert mapping, NetLoader EPLB
fallback, and MXFP8 GMM weight-list consumption remain covered.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: Existing configuration and
shared-component error-path tests ran.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: Tests exercise the retained
mapping, dispatch, and weight-loading contracts.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: Not applicable; removes retired V1 EPLB
branches and unused MoE input fields without changing V2 kernels, graph
capture, or operator dispatch.

-msgid "Expert Load Balance (EPLB)"
-msgstr "专家负载均衡 (EPLB)"
-
-msgid "Overview"
-msgstr "概述"
-
-msgid ""
-"Expert balancing for MoE (Mixture of Experts) models in LLM (Large "
-"Language) serving is essential for optimal performance. Dynamically "
-"changing experts during inference can negatively impact TTFT (Time To "
-"First Token) and TPOT (Time Per Output Token) due to stop-the-world "
-"operations. SwiftBalancer enables asynchronous expert load balancing with"
-" zero-overhead expert movement, ensuring seamless service continuity."
-msgstr ""
-"在 LLM 推理服务中，MoE 模型的专家均衡对于实现最优性能至关重要。由于“全局停顿 (stop-the-"
-"world)”操作的存在，在推理过程中动态更改专家可能会对 TTFT（首词元延迟）和 "
-"TPOT（每输出词元延迟）产生负面影响。SwiftBalancer 实现了异步专家负载均衡，具备零开销的专家迁移能力，确保了服务的无缝连续性。"
-
-msgid "EPLB Effects"
-msgstr "EPLB 效果"
-
-msgid ""
-"Reduced Latency: Dynamically balances expert loads to minimize TTFT and "
-"TPOT by distributing workloads evenly across experts."
-msgstr "降低延迟：通过在专家之间均匀分配工作负载，动态平衡专家负载，从而最小化 TTFT 和 TPOT。"
-
-msgid ""
-"Enhanced Throughput: Optimizes NPU utilization, increasing token "
-"generation speed under high-concurrency scenarios."
-msgstr "提升吞吐量：优化 NPU 利用率，提高高并发场景下的词元生成速度。"
-
-msgid ""
-"Zero-Overhead Movement: Expert redistribution occurs asynchronously "
-"without interrupting ongoing inference requests."
-msgstr "零开销迁移：专家重分布过程异步进行，不会中断正在进行的推理请求。"
-
-msgid ""
-"Adaptive Scaling: Automatically adjusts to workload fluctuations while "
-"maintaining stable performance."
-msgstr "自适应缩放：自动调整以应对工作负载波动，同时保持性能稳定。"
-
-msgid ""
-"Fault Tolerance: Redundant expert placement ensures system resilience "
-"during hardware failures."
-msgstr "容错性：冗余的专家放置策略确保了系统在硬件故障时的恢复能力。"
-

-msgstr "支持场景"

-msgid "SwiftBalanceEplb"

-
-msgid ""
-"Optimized for low-bandwidth environments. Supports intra-node and inter-"

-"**(Recommended)**"

 "  model combination; CPU tests cannot establish NPU storage correctness. This qualification is required when adding a\n"

 msgstr ""
+"- RFork 运行时需要 `YuanRong TransferEngine`。如果缺少该软件包，RFork 无法初始化传输后端。\n"
+"- 被发布为 RFork seed 的 worker 会绑定一个 seed HTTP 监听端口。默认 `rfork_seed_port_base=0` 时由操作系统分配端口。设置非零基端口时，每个 worker 会为主模型和 draft 模型预留相邻槽位；如果端口已被占用，或计算出的端口超过 `65535`，则回退到操作系统分配的端口。seed HTTP 端口应与 vLLM 服务端口、TransferEngine RPC 端口和 HIXL 端点范围分开。RFork 仅在 Linux 上受支持，端口冲突回退遵循 Linux `EADDRINUSE` 语义。\n"
+"- 在以下任一配置下，RFork 传输都会被完全旁路：模型通过默认加载器加载，也不会发布 seed。RFork 会注册正在使用的 NPU 权重内存并为其他实例提供服务，因此当这部分内存之后可能被释放或改写时，不能使用 RFork。旁路判断发生在创建 session 或 TransferEngine 之前，日志为 `RFork transfer is disabled when <reason> is enabled; using the default model loader.`\n"
+"    - **睡眠模式**（模型配置或 `vllm_config.model_config` 中的 `enable_sleep_mode`），因为睡眠会丢弃并重新分配权重存储。\n"
+"    - **在线权重传输**（设置了 `weight_transfer_config`），因为权重可能在加载后被替换。\n"
+"    - **EPLB**（`--enable-eplb`），因为异步专家重排会在 seed 服务启动后原地改写专家权重和放置映射。\n"
+"- 回退到默认加载器前，必须先释放 RFork seed 服务和已注册的内存。RFork 最多执行两次清理尝试（`FALLBACK_CLEANUP_MAX_ATTEMPTS`，当前为 2），两次尝试之间会短暂退避，然后才回收内存并重新运行默认加载器。对于尚未发布 seed 的接收端，待处理的旧版 `/put_seed` 不会阻止原生 finalize；但如果必要的本地清理仍然失败，张量所有者仍被保留，RFork 会抛出异常，拒绝在旧权重仍被固定时分配第二份模型；已经进入 finalized 状态的 session 也会抛出异常。这两种情况都会中止启动，而不会降级为较慢的加载。\n"
+"- [`rfork_planner.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/examples/rfork/rfork_planner.py) 只是一个简单的模拟实现。如果需要更强的调度、容量管理或生产级可用性行为，请根据 RFork seed 协议实现自己的规划器。其无鉴权的 `GET /debug/snapshot` 端点会列出所有已注册的 `seed_key` 和所有活动租约的 `USER_ID`；这些 ID 可用于续租和释放租约，因此任何能访问该 mock planner 的对象都能获取集群 key 并干扰活动分配。请确保它仅在可信网络段内可达（详见 FAQ）。\n"
+"- 规划器协议头 `SEED_REFCNT` 和 `SEED_RANK` 不承载调度语义，但目前在协议线上都不是可选字段：\n"
+"    - 发布 seed 时 `SEED_REFCNT` 始终发送为 `0`，不会用于容量决策（seed 容量由规划器配置控制）。规划器仍必须接受此请求头。\n"
+"    - `SEED_RANK` 仍是**必需**字段。如果 `/get_seed` 响应缺少该字段或其值为负数，RFork 会拒绝该响应；在发布 seed、续租、释放租约和删除 seed 的请求中都会发送该字段。规划器必须在 `/get_seed` 响应中原样返回，并在其他路由中接受它。已弃用的是将其用于兼容性决策：它重复了 seed key 中已经编码的 `tp_rank`，因此规划器应仅按 seed key 匹配，并将 `SEED_RANK` 视为 seed 身份元组中的不透明字段。\n"
+"- 每次心跳只检查 seed 服务线程是否仍在运行，不会在每个间隔发送带 key 的 HTTP 健康探测。带 key 的 `/health_check_with_key` 请求仅在服务启动期间发送，因此线程仍存活但 HTTP 监听无响应时，心跳仍可能成功。若需要区分这两种情况，请在网络层面监控已发布的 seed 端口。如果线程退出，RFork 会停止发送心跳，并在规划器支持删除时尝试撤销该 seed 广告。单次心跳故障本身不会停止 seed HTTP 服务；该服务由关闭或回退清理流程处理。如果删除不受支持或状态未知，RFork 会保留已发布 seed 的已注册内存和存储所有者，直到之后确认撤销且原生清理成功，或进程退出，同时保持已加载模型可继续推理。\n"
+"- 临时的规划器故障不会停止推理。可重试的初始发布和租约释放会在后台继续。受支持的删除只会在有界重试或后续清理中重试；其他删除失败会保留 HTTP 服务和已注册内存，以便重试。永久性的规划器拒绝则会阻止 seed 晋升。故障日志仅记录首次失败、周期性摘要和恢复事件。\n"
+"- 对于新支持的 NPU 格式，应在目标 NPU 和模型组合上验证传输准确性及逻辑负载契约；CPU 测试无法证明 NPU 存储的正确性。新增格式时必须进行这项验证，但这不表示运行时需要复制张量声明负载之外的分配器或描述符填充。"

Add pipeline parallel support status to the text-generation and
multimodal model tables.

Documentation only.

Verified that removing the PP column reproduces the upstream file
exactly. Checked all 70 PP values in the rendered model tables. `git
diff --check` passed.

[Doc] Update DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 950DT PD and Memcache recipes (#23365)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Update the existing DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 950DT DP8/TP1 Prefill and Decode
recipes, including the Memcache variant, with the maintained external DP
launcher, MegaMoE shared-expert fusion, and the V2 KV-transfer
connector.

- Enable `enable_fused_mc2: 3` on both roles and document its
`cann_ops_transformer` dependency. Set independent shared-expert
multistream overlap to `false`, matching the effective configuration
when fusion is active.
- Enable Prefill EPLB with the STAIR policy, 16 redundant experts, and a
64-step window / 128-step interval for short benchmarks; document the
production 1000/3000 alternative.
- Enable fastokens and four renderer workers per API server. Use
`MooncakeConnectorV2` and update the PCP/wide-EP notes for its topology
handshake.
- Set `--max-num-batched-tokens` to `8192` on Prefill and `384` on
Decode; enable local prefix caching on both roles. Keep 64 Decode
sequences, DSpark with five speculative tokens, graph execution, combine
quantization mode 4, and the recompute scheduler.
- Use layerwise Memcache access on Prefill and bulk access on Decode.
Enable Prefill local prefix caching and provide a separate external-pool
verification procedure to avoid treating HBM hits as evidence of
Memcache reuse.
- Simplify the 950DT Memcache startup examples by removing manual
`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` exports and the unused `MEMCACHE_INSTALL_PATH` input
and setup instructions.
- Retain `dram.size = 25GB` and `max.dram.size = 25GB` in Memcache.
Document optional SSD caching with portable device placeholders,
disk-initialization behavior, and per-node memory accounting.
- Embed the current official
`examples/external_online_dp/launch_online_dp.py`, aligned with #22747,
and match the presentation in #22727: uppercase inputs grouped at the
top, a positional-argument table, multiline EPLB configuration, and
reused PD launch commands for Memcache. All four role templates consume
TP/PCP/PP as arguments 7/8/9. PP defaults to 1 in the examples but
remains configurable through `--pp-size` and `--pipeline-parallel-size
$9`.

Preserved in both ordinary PD and pooled recipes:

- `HCCL_EXEC_TIMEOUT=3600` on both roles.
- Prefill `multistream_engram_overlap: false`.

The A2/A3 recipes, model checkpoint/quantization, DP8/TP1 topology, and
existing endpoint mapping are unchanged. No `PYTHONHASHSEED` exports,
benchmark-specific profiler paths, or developer-server flags are added.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Documentation only: update the configuration examples in the existing
950DT deployment tutorial. Runtime defaults, APIs, and model
implementations are unchanged. No release-note fragment is included, and
no measured performance improvement is claimed.

### How was this patch tested?

- All 14 shell blocks in the updated 950DT sections passed `bash -n`.
- Verified that the embedded launcher exactly matches the repository
source and passes Python AST parsing.
- All 21 configuration JSON objects parsed successfully.
- Executed the four documented shell templates with a stub `vllm`
command and TP=2, PCP=3, PP=4 to verify positional-argument forwarding,
including a nondefault PP size, without NPU inference.
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests/ut/examples -p
test_launch_online_dp.py -v`: all 13 existing launcher tests passed on
Windows with Git Bash.
- Verified the four role templates against the requested preserved
settings and the Prefill/Decode-specific configuration. Confirmed that
content outside the two 950DT sections is unchanged except for the
corresponding Connector name in the limitations section.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `DOCS_LANG=en bash tools/rtd_build.sh` passed with the repository's
`--strict` build configuration.
- Ran `pre-commit run --from-ref
5e4e3a22f1a95bcd6d61d0389bb390067899076a --to-ref HEAD --hook-stage
manual`. All applicable formatting/spelling checks passed. The only
failed hook was the Gitleaks shell wrapper (`/bin/bash` is unavailable
to the native Windows runner); a separate native Gitleaks scan of the
complete PR commit range with the repository configuration passed with
no leaks.

950DT/NPU validation: **CI testing only**. These revised scripts were
not executed on hardware. Two-node startup, generation, EPLB
redistribution, P-to-D transfer, layerwise Memcache reads/writes and
external hits, optional SSD caching, and accuracy/performance
qualification remain pending. Previously collected benchmark figures do
not validate this exact configuration and are not included as results
for this PR.

---

### Checklist

Documentation validation is listed above. Runtime test items are not
claimed for this documentation-only change.

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves boundary conditions and added applicable runtime coverage.
- [ ] **Regression test**: Added a regression test that fails without
the change, where applicable.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: Covered applicable runtime
error paths.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: Added applicable behavior-focused
runtime tests.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: Attached comparative hardware benchmarks
and performance regression coverage.

@@ -359,12 +359,26 @@ vLLM Ascend revision.
     Use the 950DT runtime from [Section 4.1](#41-docker-image-installation)
     on both nodes. Prefill requires native SWA bounded replay with the PD connector.
 
-    Both roles use DSpark with five speculative tokens and enable shared-expert
-    multistream overlap. Prefill runs the target and draft models in eager mode
-    and sets `multistream_engram_overlap: false`. Decode uses
-    `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` for the target model and the default draft graph execution,
-    with `combine_quant_mode: 4` and the recompute scheduler. The examples use
-    the 950DT defaults for CPU binding, DSA overlap, and Decode Engram overlap.
+    Both roles use DSpark with five speculative tokens and
+    `enable_fused_mc2: 3` for MegaMoE with shared-expert fusion. This mode requires
+    `cann_ops_transformer` in both containers. The shared expert runs inside
+    MegaMoE, so set `multistream_overlap_shared_expert: false`.
+    Prefill runs the target and draft models in eager mode and keeps
+    `multistream_engram_overlap: false`. Decode uses `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` for the
+    target model and the default draft graph execution, with
+    `combine_quant_mode: 4` and the recompute scheduler. The examples use the
+    950DT defaults for CPU binding, DSA overlap, and Decode Engram overlap.
+
+    Both roles enable `VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1` and require `fastokens>=0.3.5`.
+    `--renderer-num-workers 4` starts four input-rendering workers per API
+    server; it does not configure the PD proxy's worker count.
+    `MooncakeConnectorV2` uses its default non-layerwise pull mode.
+
+    Prefill enables EPLB with the `stair` policy and 16 redundant experts across
+    the EP group. The `64`-step load window and `128`-step rearrangement interval
+    suit short benchmarks. For production, use `window_size: 1000` and
